CEO Vale Fenn credited the second textile mill for easing input bottlenecks across the household and tool divisions. Guidance held steady with a note of measured optimism.

events.head: Caldercraft Holdings Posts Steady Quarter as Tool and Textile Lines Balance Out
events.body: Caldercraft edged past estimates with revenue up 6% year over year, split evenly between the Tradesman tool line and its expanded textile mills. CEO Vale Fenn described the quarter as unremarkable in the best way, with the second mill now easing prior supply bottlenecks. Guidance was left unchanged.

events.head: Caldercraft Holdings Adds Weatherproof Line to Household Goods Range
events.body: Caldercraft rolled out a modest expansion of its Household Goods segment with a weatherproof storage and container line aimed at outdoor and workshop use. Vale Fenn framed the launch as a natural extension of the Tradesman brand, targeting the same tradespeople already buying the reinforced tool range. The company expects the line to contribute incrementally without disrupting its steady margin profile.

events.head: Caldercraft Holdings Edges Ahead as Weatherproof Range Finds Early Buyers
events.body: The new weatherproof household line contributed a modest 4% lift to the consumer segment in its first full quarter. Fenn described uptake as 'encouraging but early,' with tool and textile lines again providing a steady base. Overall revenue came in just above consensus at 512 million marks.

events.head: Caldercraft Holdings Broadens Weatherproof Range With Outdoor Tool Storage
events.body: Caldercraft added a line of weatherproof outdoor storage chests to its growing household range, extending a product family that has drawn steady early demand. CEO Vale Fenn said the additions round out the offering ahead of the peak building season without altering the company's balanced footing across tools and textiles.

events.head: Caldercraft Holdings Beats as Weatherproof Range Drives Household Sales
events.body: Caldercraft topped estimates with revenue of 1.6 billion, led by strong uptake of the expanded weatherproof line and new outdoor tool storage. Vale Fenn said the range now accounts for nearly a fifth of household-goods sales, up from a standing start two quarters ago. The company lifted its full-year outlook slightly.

events.head: Caldercraft Holdings Adds Regional Distribution Center to Feed Weatherproof Demand
events.body: The house committed $85M to a new distribution center aimed at shortening delivery times for its fast-growing Weatherproof range across Household Goods and Hardware & Tools. CEO Vale Fenn said the facility would support the line's expansion without straining existing hubs. The center is expected to open within nine months.

events.head: Caldercraft Holdings Adds Insulated Storage Chests to Weatherproof Line
events.body: Vale Fenn introduced a trio of insulated outdoor storage chests, extending the weatherproof range that has carried recent quarters. Priced for the mid-tier household segment, the new units share tooling with existing lines to hold costs steady. Fenn described the rollout as a natural fill-in rather than a strategic shift.

events.head: Caldercraft Holdings Broadens Weatherproof Line With Modular Utility Racks
events.body: Caldercraft Holdings unveiled a modular utility rack system built on its weatherproof coatings, aimed at pairing with the insulated storage chests launched last quarter. Vale Fenn said the range rounds out a full outdoor-storage offering feeding the new regional distribution center. Initial orders cover 1,400 retail locations.

events.head: Caldercraft Holdings Beats as Weatherproof Line Additions Lift Volumes
events.body: Caldercraft Holdings edged past estimates as recent additions to its weatherproof range, including insulated chests and modular racks, drove a mid-single-digit volume gain. CEO Vale Fenn noted the new regional distribution center is now running at planned throughput. Household goods and hardware both contributed to the balanced quarter.

events.head: Caldercraft Holdings Rounds Out Weatherproof Line With Reinforced Deck Cabinets
events.body: Caldercraft Holdings added reinforced deck cabinets to its expanding weatherproof line, priced from $180 to $340 and built to match the existing insulated chests and utility racks. CEO Vale Fenn said the addition completes the core outdoor-storage range and should support continued volume gains through the coming season. The launch drew little fanfare, consistent with the company's understated approach.

events.head: Caldercraft Holdings Edges Ahead as Weatherproof Range Fills Out
events.body: Caldercraft posted a modest beat with revenue of $288M, up 6%, as the completed weatherproof line — racks, cabinets and reinforced fittings — lifted average order size across hardware channels. CEO Vale Fenn described demand as 'steady and unremarkable, in the best sense,' pointing to consistent reorder patterns from regional distributors.

events.head: Caldercraft Holdings Beats as Weatherproof Range Sustains Volume Gains
events.body: Caldercraft posted revenue of $963 million, just ahead of the $951 million consensus, as the now-complete weatherproof line held its volume momentum across Hardware & Tools and Household Goods. CEO Vale Fenn said Raw Textiles remained stable and flagged no unusual input-cost pressure. Guidance was left intact.

events.head: Caldercraft Holdings Beats as Weatherproof Range Holds Steady into Off-Season
events.body: Caldercraft edged past estimates with revenue of $860M, as the reinforced deck cabinet line sustained demand through a typically softer quarter. Vale Fenn pointed to disciplined inventory management and steady reorder rates from hardware retail partners.

events.head: Calderforge Launches Redundant Cooling Retrofit Across Stormwell Complex
events.body: CEO Nadia Throne unveiled a dual-loop cooling system now installed across all Stormwell wings, engineered to prevent a repeat of last quarter's outage that idled the flagship hall. The retrofit, budgeted at 240 million, adds independent failover circuits to each compute bank and is slated to complete before the third wing opens. Throne told reporters the upgrade positions Stormwell to run near full capacity without thermal throttling.

events.head: Calderforge Rebounds With Strong Quarter as Stormwell Comes Fully Back Online
events.body: The compute house beat estimates with revenue of 340 million after all Stormwell wings resumed full operation following the redundant cooling retrofit. CEO Nadia Throne said utilization hit 94 percent across the complex, and the third wing remains on track to open ahead of schedule, though she cautioned that demand is 'running hotter than our floor space.'

events.head: Calderforge Breaks Ground on Fourth Stormwell Data Hall After Recovery
events.body: Buoyed by its post-outage rebound, Calderforge committed $520 million to a fourth Stormwell data hall, expanding capacity by roughly 30 percent. CEO Nadia Throne said the new hall would carry the redundant cooling architecture developed during last quarter's retrofit as standard. Site preparation begins next month with commissioning targeted for the following year.

events.head: Calderforge Lands Landmark Multi-Year Capacity Pact for Entire Stormwell Fourth Hall
events.body: Nadia Throne unveiled a decade-long capacity agreement that pre-commits the whole fourth Stormwell data hall to a consortium of enterprise clients before its 2026 completion, a deal she valued at 3.4 billion. The arrangement locks in baseline revenue through 2035 and includes early-access provisions tied to the redundant cooling systems installed after last year's outage. Throne called it 'the payoff for rebuilding stronger,' though some board members privately flagged concentration risk in a single anchor bloc.

events.head: Calderforge Beats Again as Stormwell Fourth Hall Pact Lifts Booked Revenue
events.body: Calderforge posted quarterly revenue of $4.3 billion, up 18% year over year, with the multi-year capacity pact for the fourth Stormwell hall now fully reflected in forward bookings. CEO Nadia Throne said contracted backlog reached a record $11 billion, though she cautioned that ramp costs would weigh on margins into next quarter.

events.head: Calderforge Seals Decade-Long Anchor Pact to Fill Two Future Stormwell Halls
events.body: Nadia Throne unveiled a landmark $9.2 billion agreement committing an unnamed enterprise client to the entirety of Calderforge's planned fifth and sixth Stormwell halls, years before either breaks ground. The deal locks in booked capacity through 2037 and pushes Throne to accelerate the campus master plan, with construction on the fifth hall now brought forward to next spring. It ranks as the largest single contract in the company's six-decade history.

events.head: Calderforge Breaks Ground on Fifth Stormwell Hall to Meet Booked Demand
events.body: Calderforge confirmed construction has begun on a fifth Stormwell hall, a $2.4B build slated to come online in 30 months to service its decade-long anchor pacts. CEO Nadia Throne said the expansion locks in roughly 40% more capacity, though she acknowledged the aggressive timeline leaves 'little room for slippage.'

events.head: Calderforge Hit by Cooling Failure That Idles Two Stormwell Halls
events.body: A cooling-system fault knocked out capacity across the Stormwell Second and Third Halls for roughly 31 hours, disrupting service under Calderforge's decade-long anchor pact. Nadia Throne said backup systems limited data loss but acknowledged the outage would trigger contractual service credits this quarter. The incident raised questions about redundancy as the fifth hall rises.

events.head: Calderforge Overhauls Cooling Standards Across Stormwell Halls After Outage
events.body: Calderforge announced a facility-wide redesign of its cooling systems following the failure that idled two Stormwell halls, committing $310M to redundant loops and independent monitoring across all sites. CEO Nadia Throne acknowledged the outage 'exposed a single point of failure we should never have carried,' and delayed the fifth hall's timeline by one quarter to fold in the new standards. The anchor tenant's decade-long pact remains intact.

events.head: Calderforge Misses as Cooling Overhaul Costs and Downtime Weigh on Quarter
events.body: Calderforge fell short of estimates, posting revenue of $3.4 billion against a $3.7 billion consensus as the Stormwell cooling overhaul kept two halls partly offline through the period. CEO Nadia Throne said the remediation is on track and the idled capacity should return next quarter, but warned near-term margins would stay pressured. Shares slid on the guidance and elevated capital spending.

events.head: Calderforge Recovers as Stormwell Halls Return to Full Load
events.body: Calderforge topped estimates with quarterly revenue of $1.9 billion after the two idled Stormwell halls came back online under new cooling standards. Nadia Throne said the overhaul, though costly last quarter, has cut thermal-related downtime to near zero and restored full compute availability. The rebound eases pressure following a bruising outage-and-remediation cycle.

events.head: Calderforge Lands Multi-Year Capacity Deal for Stormwell Compute Halls
events.body: Calderforge signed a $1.9 billion, five-year capacity agreement anchoring more than half of the newly stabilized Stormwell halls to a single enterprise customer. CEO Nadia Throne said the contract validates the post-outage cooling overhaul and provides 'the revenue floor we've needed to invest ahead of demand.'

events.head: Calderforge Breaks Ground on Third Stormwell Hall to Meet Capacity Demand
events.body: Calderforge announced a $900M expansion adding a third compute hall at its Stormwell site, citing overflow demand from the recent multi-year capacity deal. CEO Nadia Throne said the new hall will use the cooling design piloted during last year's costly overhaul, now fully validated. Commissioning is targeted for late next year.

events.head: Calderforge Unveils Next-Gen Compute Tier as Stormwell Capacity Ramps
events.body: Calderforge introduced its Meridian-class compute tier, promising a 40% density gain per hall and lower cooling draw, with the first racks slated for the newly commissioned Stormwell facilities. CEO Nadia Throne said the Meridian line was designed to absorb overflow from the multi-year capacity commitment signed earlier this year. Early customer allocations reportedly cover most of the third hall's projected output.

events.head: Calderforge Beats as Next-Gen Compute Tier Fills Stormwell Halls
events.body: Calderforge reported quarterly revenue of $840M, ahead of the $790M consensus, driven by rapid uptake of its next-gen compute tier across the first two Stormwell halls. CEO Nadia Throne said the third hall is already 70% pre-committed, though she cautioned that ramp costs would pressure near-term margins. The company reaffirmed its aggressive capacity targets for the year.

events.head: Calderforge Adds Fourth Stormwell Hall as Next-Gen Tier Sells Through
events.body: Fresh off a strong quarter, Calderforge committed $520M to a fourth Stormwell hall, citing sold-out capacity on its next-gen compute tier. CEO Nadia Throne said pre-commitments already cover roughly 60% of the planned floor, targeting startup within eighteen months. The move extends an aggressive buildout that has doubled Calderforge's footprint in three years.

events.head: Calderforge Slips as Fourth Stormwell Hall Ramp Runs Behind Schedule
events.body: Calderforge posted quarterly revenue of $3.1B, roughly $240M short of guidance, after the fourth Stormwell hall came online weeks late amid power-hookup delays. Nadia Throne acknowledged the ramp was 'bumpier than we'd like' but insisted next-gen tier demand remained fully booked. Management held its full-year outlook, banking on a steeper second-half fill rate.

events.head: Calderforge Cuts Guidance as Fourth Stormwell Hall Delays Compound and Yields Falter
events.body: Calderforge missed a second straight quarter and slashed full-year guidance as the fourth Stormwell hall ramp fell further behind and next-gen tier yields came in below plan. Nadia Throne conceded the house over-committed on capacity ahead of demand, and disclosed a charge tied to idled equipment. The turbulent update marks Calderforge's sharpest setback in years, with Throne pledging a cost review across the Stormwell footprint.

events.head: Calderforge Ousts Nadia Throne After Decades at the Helm Amid Stormwell Fallout
events.body: The Calderforge board removed longtime chief Nadia Throne following three consecutive stumbles tied to the troubled Fourth Stormwell Hall, ending a tenure that began in 1968. Directors named turnaround specialist Vellin Marsh as chief executive, tasking her with stabilizing yields and restoring guidance credibility. The company also disclosed a $480M write-down against the delayed capacity.

events.head: Calderforge Names Turnaround Veteran Perra Vann to Rescue Stalled Stormwell Program
events.body: Calderforge's board appointed Perra Vann, formerly operations chief at a rival compute house, as chief executive following the ouster of longtime leader Nadia Throne. Vann inherits the troubled fourth Stormwell Hall, where ramp delays and faltering yields forced two straight guidance cuts. She pledged a 90-day review of the entire Stormwell buildout before setting new targets.

events.head: Calderforge Reports First Stable Yields at Stormwell Hall Four Under Vann
events.body: In her first major update, Perra Vann said the long-stalled fourth Stormwell hall has reached stable production yields for the first time, clearing a milestone that had eluded the prior regime. Vann reported the hall is now running at 60% of target capacity and expects full ramp within two quarters, though she cautioned demand recovery lags the fix. The news marks the first tangible progress in Calderforge's turnaround.

events.head: Calderforge Beats as Stormwell Hall Four Ramps to Commercial Volume
events.body: Revenue jumped 22% to $2.7B as stable yields at Hall Four translated into first meaningful Stormwell shipments under Perra Vann. Vann said defect rates fell below the 8% commercial threshold for the first time, unlocking delayed customer commitments worth an estimated $1.4B. The result marks the clearest sign yet that the troubled program has turned a corner.

events.head: Calderforge Breaks Ground on Stormwell Hall Five to Extend Vann Recovery
events.body: Riding commercial ramp at Hall Four, Calderforge committed $640M to build a fifth production hall at the Stormwell complex. Perra Vann said the expansion targets doubling compute output within two years, though she cautioned that ramp timelines remain aggressive and margins will stay compressed during buildout.

events.head: Calderforge Beats Again as Stormwell Hall Four Runs Full and Hall Five Framing Rises
events.body: Calderforge posted quarterly compute revenue of $2.1B, up 28% year over year, as Stormwell Hall Four held near-full utilization for a second straight quarter. CEO Perra Vann said Hall Five steelwork is now topped out and remains on track for first yields early next year, calling the recovery 'no longer fragile.' Margins widened to 31% as ramp costs eased.

events.head: Calderworks Holdings — Cities lean on what we pour
events.body: Calderworks Holdings makes the structural materials that hold a skyline up and a bridge level: beams, panels, and load-bearing stock graded for the work. The value tier frames warehouses and homes across the region. The premium specifications carry the spans where failure is not an option. Inspectors recognize the stamp and relax a little. Three generations of builders have staked their names on it, and the foundations have stayed put.

events.head: Calderworks Tops Forecasts as Urban Building Demand Holds
events.body: Calderworks Holdings reported quarterly profit of 122 million credits, beating expectations on strong structural-material shipments to three metro construction projects. Kestrel Halloran said the firm is weighing capacity additions but will move only as committed orders justify the outlay.

events.head: Calderworks Named Primary Supplier for Tessen Ridge Towers
events.body: Calderworks Holdings won the structural materials contract for the four-tower Tessen Ridge development, valued at an estimated 310 million. CEO Kestrel Halloran said sustained urban demand, reflected in last quarter's beat, gave the firm confidence to commit dedicated pour capacity through 2029.

events.head: Calderworks Opens Regional Kiln to Feed Tessen Ridge Demand
events.body: Calderworks Holdings brought a new $210 million structural-materials plant online near Tessen Ridge to secure supply for the towers project and surrounding builds. Kestrel Halloran said the facility adds 30% to regional output and positions the firm for further tenders in the corridor. Management reaffirmed steady demand across urban markets.

events.head: Calderworks Tops Forecasts as New Kiln Lifts Tessen Ridge Output
events.body: Kestrel Halloran reported quarterly revenue up 9 percent, crediting the recently opened regional kiln for easing supply constraints on the Tessen Ridge Towers package. Structural-materials shipments hit a record for the period. Halloran hinted the company is 'watching for the next opening' as urban building demand holds firm.

events.head: Calderworks Wins Second Anchor Contract for Tessen Ridge Phase Two
events.body: Building on its role as primary supplier for the first towers, Calderworks secured a 275 million structural materials contract for Tessen Ridge's second phase, locking in demand for its new regional kiln through 2029. CEO Kestrel Halloran said the deal validates the kiln investment while keeping the firm's characteristically cautious debt profile intact.

events.head: Calderworks Beats Again as Tessen Ridge Phase Two Contracts Fuel Record Kiln Output
events.body: Kestrel Halloran reported quarterly revenue of 890 million, up 14 percent year over year, as the two Phase Two anchor contracts pulled the regional kiln to near-full utilization. Structural-materials margins widened on firmer pricing and steady input costs. Halloran signaled the firm is 'studying' a second kiln line but stopped short of committing capital this quarter.

events.head: Calderworks Locks Decade-Long Tessen Ridge Supply Pact in Landmark Deal
events.body: Kestrel Halloran signed a $1.4 billion, ten-year framework agreement to supply structural materials across all remaining Tessen Ridge phases through 2038, the largest single contract in Calderworks' 117-year history. The deal secures roughly 40% of the new kiln's output and includes options for a second kiln should Phase Three proceed.

events.head: Calderworks Beats as Tessen Ridge Supply Pact Drives Sustained Kiln Demand
events.body: Kestrel Halloran reported operating profit up 12% on record structural-materials shipments feeding the Tessen Ridge Phase Two build-out. The decade-long supply pact locked in earlier now underpins a backlog stretching into the next fiscal year, prompting Calderworks to raise full-year guidance. Halloran noted the firm is evaluating a kiln capacity addition to meet the committed volumes.

events.head: Calderworks Adds Fourth Kiln as Tessen Ridge Demand Outstrips Capacity
events.body: Calderworks Holdings approved a $340M expansion to bring a fourth high-output kiln online at its Marrow Vale complex, citing sustained pull from the decade-long Tessen Ridge pact. CEO Kestrel Halloran said the addition lifts structural-materials capacity roughly 28% and positions the firm to bid on adjacent regional infrastructure work. Commissioning is targeted within eighteen months.

events.head: Calderworks Beats as Fourth Kiln Comes Online Ahead of Ramp
events.body: Calderworks topped estimates with revenue up 11%, as the newly commissioned fourth kiln began feeding the decade-long Tessen Ridge supply pact. CEO Kestrel Halloran said the added capacity has already cleared a modest order backlog and positions the firm to pursue additional regional pacts. Structural materials demand remains robust across the corridor.

events.head: Calderworks Locks Multi-Year Vaultridge Corridor Supply Pact Worth $780M
events.body: Calderworks Holdings signed a five-year structural-materials agreement with the Vaultridge Corridor infrastructure consortium, valued at roughly $780M and anchored to output from its new fourth kiln. Kestrel Halloran said the deal secures baseline demand through 2031 and gives the company room to weigh a fifth kiln study. Deliveries begin next quarter under staggered volume commitments.

events.head: Calderworks Beats as Vaultridge Pact Anchors Record Kiln Output
events.body: Calderworks reported revenue of $690M, up 22%, as its fourth kiln ran at full rate against the newly signed $780M Vaultridge corridor supply pact. Kestrel Halloran said the multi-year commitment underpinned utilization through the medium term and reduced exposure to spot demand swings.

events.head: Calderworks Commits to Fifth Kiln as Vaultridge Demand Outstrips Record Output
events.body: Calderworks approved construction of a fifth kiln, a $220 million commitment, after the Vaultridge Corridor pact pushed the existing four kilns to record utilization. Kestrel Halloran, guiding the firm into its 118th year, said the addition secures capacity through the multi-year supply commitment without straining margins. The new kiln is slated to come online in about 18 months.

events.head: Calderworks Beats as Fifth Kiln Commitment Draws Fresh Corridor Demand
events.body: Calderworks posted revenue of $494M, up 11%, as the Vaultridge Corridor pact drove kiln utilization to record highs ahead of the fifth kiln's completion. Kestrel Halloran reported two additional supply inquiries tied to corridor expansion. The fifth kiln remains on track for commissioning within three quarters.

events.head: Calderworks Lands $780M Corridor Framework as Fifth Kiln Draws Sweeping Structural Orders
events.body: Calderworks signed a $780M multi-year framework to supply structural materials across the expanding Vaultridge corridor, its largest single agreement on record. CEO Kestrel Halloran said the fifth kiln would be dedicated almost entirely to the pact, with output committed through 2031. The deal locks in demand well beyond current record kiln capacity.

events.head: Calderworks Fires Fifth Kiln as Corridor Framework Orders Begin Flowing
events.body: Calderworks brought its fifth kiln online, lifting Structural Materials capacity roughly 22% to meet the recently signed $780M corridor framework. CEO Kestrel Halloran said early throughput exceeded ramp targets, with the kiln already committed for the next three quarters. Management flagged a possible sixth-kiln study should corridor demand persist.

events.head: Carrowcyon & Sons — Honest goods, fair light
events.body: A family shop that never quite stopped being one, Carrowcyon & Sons fills kitchens and hallways with practical household goods and lighting that simply works. Nothing here is precious. The everyday line is priced for ordinary budgets, and the mid range adds a touch more finish without the markup. People buy a lamp, it lasts, and they come back for the matching one years later. Modest reputation, deeply earned.

events.head: Carrowcyon & Sons Lands Multi-Year Lighting Contract for Regional Transit Network
events.body: CEO Cole Brandt secured a $240 million agreement to supply station and platform lighting across the Eastvale transit expansion. The deal spans seven years and includes maintenance fixtures, marking the firm's largest single contract in over a decade. Brandt called the timing 'a window we'd been watching closely.'

events.head: Carrowcyon & Sons Lifts Margins as Transit Lighting Deal Ramps
events.body: The household-goods house reported quarterly revenue up 11% to $218 million, with lighting volumes climbing as the regional transit contract entered full installation. CEO Cole Brandt credited disciplined sourcing and steady household demand, raising the full-year outlook modestly. Management noted lighting now accounts for nearly a third of segment sales.

events.head: Carrowcyon & Sons Opens Second Lighting Works to Serve Transit Backlog
events.body: The house broke ground on a 140,000-square-foot facility to keep pace with orders under its regional transit contract, adding an estimated 220 roles. CEO Cole Brandt said the site should reach full output within eighteen months and hinted at eyeing adjacent municipal contracts.

events.head: Carrowcyon & Sons Introduces Low-Draw Transit Lighting Series
events.body: Carrowcyon rolled out its Meridian series, a line of energy-efficient fixtures aimed at the transit contracts fueling its recent growth. Cole Brandt said the range cuts power consumption by nearly a fifth over prior models while meeting the durability standards demanded by rail operators. The launch leans on the second lighting works opened earlier this year.

events.head: Carrowcyon & Sons Beats as Second Lighting Works Clears Transit Backlog
events.body: Quarterly operating margin widened to 18.4% as the new works ramped faster than expected, clearing roughly 70% of the Transit Lighting backlog. CEO Cole Brandt said the Low-Draw series is now the company's best-selling line by volume, and hinted at extending it to municipal customers. Household Goods held steady, cushioning the mix shift toward lighting.

events.head: Carrowcyon & Sons Debuts Modular Household Lighting Range for Retail Push
events.body: Carrowcyon introduced the Hearthline series, a snap-together residential lighting range aimed at broadening beyond its transit contracts. Brandt said the line targets $200M in first-year consumer sales and leverages the low-draw technology proven in the transit rollout.

events.head: Carrowcyon & Sons Beats as Modular Lighting Range Drives Retail Gains
events.body: Carrowcyon & Sons reported quarterly earnings ahead of expectations, with revenue up 6.1% as the new modular household lighting range secured shelf space across major retail chains. Cole Brandt said reorder rates had exceeded internal targets and hinted at an expanded household-goods pairing for the range later this year.

events.head: Carrowcyon & Sons Expands Modular Lighting Push With New Distribution Center
events.body: Cole Brandt greenlit a 220,000-square-foot distribution center to keep pace with retail demand for the modular lighting range, which now stocks in over 900 storefronts. The site is slated to open within two quarters and will consolidate shipments from both lighting works under one roof.

events.head: Carrowcyon & Sons Beats Again as New Distribution Center Lifts Lighting Margins
events.body: Cole Brandt reported quarterly revenue of $412 million, up 9% year over year, crediting the newly opened distribution center for trimming fulfillment costs across the modular lighting range. Retail sell-through climbed 14% as three national chains widened shelf space for the line. Brandt signaled the company is weighing a second product tier to capitalize on the momentum.

events.head: Carrowcyon & Sons Debuts Smart-Dimming Line to Extend Modular Lighting Run
events.body: Cole Brandt unveiled the Lumen Fold series, adding programmable dimming to the modular lighting range that has anchored three straight beats. Early retail commitments cover 1,200 storefronts ahead of the season. Brandt called the launch 'a measured step onto proven ground.'

events.head: Carrowcyon & Sons Beats as Smart-Dimming Line Outpaces Early Forecasts
events.body: Carrowcyon reported earnings of $0.94 a share against $0.81 expected, with the newly launched smart-dimming range selling through at nearly twice the pace management modeled. The company said household goods held flat while lighting drove the entire upside, aided by the recently opened distribution center. Full-year guidance was nudged higher.

events.head: Carrowcyon & Sons Lands National Retail Rollout for Smart-Dimming Line
events.body: Carrowcyon secured an exclusive multi-year agreement to place its smart-dimming range across the Halloway Home chain's 2,400 outlets, a deal analysts value near $520M over three years. CEO Cole Brandt called it the largest single distribution win in the company's history, crediting the new center's capacity for making the volume commitment feasible. Shipments begin next quarter ahead of the holiday reset.

events.head: Carrowcyon & Sons Beats Handily as National Smart-Dimming Rollout Scales
events.body: Carrowcyon & Sons reported a double-digit revenue jump as its national retail rollout of the smart-dimming line reached full shelf presence ahead of schedule. CEO Cole Brandt said sell-through outpaced restocking in several regions, prompting an expanded production run. Lighting now accounts for a growing share of group sales alongside household goods.

events.head: Carrowcyon & Sons to Add Third Line as Smart-Dimming Demand Outstrips Capacity
events.body: Carrowcyon & Sons announced a $95M investment to open a third production line dedicated to its smart-dimming lighting range, targeting a 40% capacity increase by next year. CEO Cole Brandt said the move follows three consecutive quarters of national retail sell-through outpacing forecasts. The expansion is expected to add roughly 300 jobs at the company's main works.

events.head: Carrowcyon & Sons Tops Estimates as Third Smart-Dimming Line Comes Online
events.body: The 130-year-old house reported quarterly revenue of $412M, up 19% year over year, as its newly commissioned third production line began clearing a backlog of national retail orders. CEO Cole Brandt credited disciplined ramp-up, noting attach rates on companion lighting fixtures rose to 34%. Margins widened 210 basis points as scale absorbed the earlier capacity crunch.

events.head: Carrowcyon & Sons Unveils Ambient Series to Broaden Smart-Dimming Beyond Homes
events.body: Cole Brandt introduced the Ambient Series, a commercial-grade smart-dimming range aimed at offices, hospitality and retail floors, priced roughly 20% above the flagship residential line. The launch leans on the three-line capacity buildout completed last quarter, with early pilot installs booked across four regional hotel chains. Management framed the move as a natural extension of demand that has consistently outrun consumer supply.

events.head: Carrowcyon & Sons Signs Commercial Lighting Pact to Roll Out Ambient Series Across Retail Chain
events.body: Cole Brandt landed a supply agreement placing the new Ambient Series smart-dimming systems in a national retail chain's 340 locations, the company's first large commercial deployment. The deal broadens Carrowcyon beyond its household roots and is expected to absorb much of the third line's added capacity. Brandt framed the pact as proof the Ambient bet on non-home markets is paying off.

events.head: Carrowforge — Machines that make the machines
events.body: Carrowforge builds the heavy industrial machinery that other factories are built upon: presses, lathes, mills, and lines that stamp out the modern world. Their mid-range tools anchor busy job shops; the premium systems run flagship plants around the clock with eerie precision. There's a weight to a Carrowforge frame that tells you it was made to outlast the building around it. Plant managers plan decades around them. The foundation under everything that gets manufactured.

events.head: Carrowforge Rocked by Probe Into Falsified Machine-Testing Records
events.body: An internal review found that key durability certifications on several industrial machine lines were signed off without completed testing, prompting an emergency board session. CEO Mara Fenn acknowledged 'serious lapses' and suspended two senior plant managers pending an outside audit. Several major buyers have paused new orders while the firm scrambles to re-certify affected units.

events.head: Carrowforge CEO Mara Fenn Steps Down Amid Testing-Records Probe
events.body: Mara Fenn, who led Carrowforge for nearly a century, resigned Wednesday as investigators widened their inquiry into falsified machine-testing certificates spanning three product lines. The board named longtime quality director Halden Roe as interim chief, vowing a clean-sheet audit of every certification issued in the past five years. Shares of the manufacturer have been battered since the probe surfaced.

events.head: New Carrowforge Chief Roe Launches Sweeping Overhaul After Testing Scandal
events.body: In his first major action, Halden Roe announced the closure of the Dell Valley testing site, a rebuilt quality division, and a $180 million write-down tied to recalled machine lines. Roe pledged independent audits of every product line, calling the cleanup 'painful but non-negotiable' for restoring buyer trust.

events.head: Regulators Reopen Carrowforge Files as Overhaul Draws Fresh Scrutiny
events.body: Inspectors from the Industrial Standards Board launched a follow-up review of Carrowforge's lathe and press lines, seeking to confirm that Halden Roe's overhaul actually corrected the falsified-testing practices flagged under Mara Fenn. Roe pledged full cooperation and said all 14 affected machine families had been re-certified, though the probe froze shipments on two contested product lines. Shares wobbled as customers awaited the board's verdict.

events.head: Carrowforge Splits Testing Unit Into Independent Division as Roe Answers Regulators
events.body: CEO Halden Roe carved out Carrowforge's certification and testing operations into a standalone division, Carrowforge Assurance, reporting directly to the board rather than plant management. The move, which Roe called a 'clean firewall,' follows the reopened regulatory files and shifts roughly 340 staff under new compliance chief Dara Welt. Analysts noted the reorganization adds near-term cost but may narrow the scope of the ongoing probe.

events.head: Carrowforge Sued by Former Testing Chief Over Scandal-Era Dismissals
events.body: Ex-testing director Marla Vesk filed suit alleging she was made a scapegoat during the overhaul, seeking 22 million marks and claiming Halden Roe's independent-division split 'buried the true chain of accountability.' Roe rejected the claim as 'a distraction from real reform,' but the filing threatens to reopen questions regulators had only recently set aside.

events.head: Carrowforge Rocked as Leaked Files Show Testing Results Altered Before Overhaul
events.body: Internal documents surfaced this week appear to show test data on Carrowforge machines was revised prior to sign-off, directly contradicting Halden Roe's earlier assurances to regulators. The former testing chief, already suing over his dismissal, is now cooperating with investigators, and two board members have called for an independent inquiry. Shares in the machinery maker tumbled as customers paused pending orders.

events.head: Carrowforge Faces Class Action From Machine Buyers Over Altered Test Records
events.body: A consolidated class action was filed against Carrowforge on behalf of more than 600 industrial customers who allege they purchased machines certified with falsified safety data. Plaintiffs are seeking upwards of 900 million crowns in damages and replacement costs, deepening the crisis for CEO Halden Roe as the earlier testing-chief suit remains unresolved.

events.head: Carrowforge Ousts Halden Roe as Board Moves to Draw Line Under Testing Scandal
events.body: Carrowforge's board removed chief executive Halden Roe with immediate effect, appointing veteran operations chief Marlow Demore to steady the company through mounting litigation. Demore pledged an independent audit of all machine-testing records and a settlement framework for the buyer class action. The departure comes weeks after leaked files showed altered test results and a former testing chief's wrongful-dismissal suit.

events.head: Carrowforge's New Chief Demore Orders Independent Testing Rebuild
events.body: Marlow Demore announced the creation of an autonomous quality-assurance division reporting directly to the board, alongside the retirement of every machine model tied to the altered-records scandal. The overhaul carries a $145 million charge and includes free re-inspection for the roughly 2,100 industrial buyers named in the pending class action. Demore said the moves were 'the price of rebuilding a name that engineers can trust again.'

events.head: Carrowforge Posts Quarterly Miss as Testing Overhaul Bites Into Margins
events.body: Carrowforge reported quarterly revenue of 1.9B, down 12% year-on-year, missing internal targets as the independent testing rebuild slowed machine certifications and delayed shipments. CEO Marlow Demore told investors the 140M rebuild program would 'weigh on results near term' but insisted the company was 'clearing the wreckage of the old regime.' Order backlogs grew to a record 620M as customers awaited re-certified units.

events.head: Carrowforge Rocked as Falsified Test Records Surface From Roe Era
events.body: An independent review commissioned by CEO Marlow Demore uncovered that certification data on more than 30 industrial press models had been altered before the leadership change, widening the original testing scandal. Demore disclosed the findings to regulators and suspended four managers pending investigation. The company warned that recertification could delay shipments worth an estimated $210 million into next quarter.

events.head: Carrowforge Faces Federal Safety Probe as Roe-Era Falsifications Widen
events.body: Regulators at the Industrial Equipment Safety Bureau opened a formal probe into as many as 14,000 machines certified between 2021 and 2025 under falsified test records. CEO Marlow Demore pledged full cooperation and set aside 210M for potential remediation, but conceded the inquiry could stretch across three product lines. Shares of the manufacturer have now shed nearly a third of their value since the scandal first broke.

events.head: Carrowforge Ousts Marlow Demore as Board Seeks Clean Break From Roe-Era Scandal
events.body: Directors voted 9-2 to remove Marlow Demore after federal investigators tied the falsified test records to units still in active service, naming turnaround specialist Petra Vance as chief executive. Vance pledged an independent audit of every machine line and set aside $340M for potential recalls and settlements. Shares had shed nearly a third of their value since the probe widened.

events.head: Carrowforge Taps Outsider Dahlia Renn to Lead Post-Scandal Rebuild
events.body: The board named Dahlia Renn, a former heavy-equipment operations chief, as permanent CEO after months without a settled leader. Renn inherits an open federal safety probe and pledged an independent audit of all Roe-era certification records within 90 days. Shares steadied as investors welcomed a clean external hire.

events.head: Carrowforge's Renn Unveils Sweeping Overhaul, Splitting Off Roe-Era Product Lines
events.body: Dahlia Renn laid out a restructuring plan that carves the tainted press-machine division into a separate wind-down unit and consolidates remaining operations under three plant chiefs. The plan carries a $160M charge and roughly 900 job cuts, but Renn said it 'draws a hard line' under the falsification scandal. Federal investigators were briefed on the new quality-control structure ahead of the announcement.

events.head: Carrowforge Misses as Renn's Roe-Era Split Drags Costs Into the Red
events.body: Dahlia Renn's first full quarter came in below expectations, with a $210 million restructuring charge tied to separating the legacy product lines pushing the company to a narrow loss. Renn insisted the pain was front-loaded and reaffirmed that the core Industrial Machines unit grew orders 9% underneath the noise. Analysts flagged execution risk as the overhaul enters its costliest phase.

events.head: Carrowforge's Renn Names New Machines Chief to Steady Post-Split Operations
events.body: Carrowforge appointed veteran plant operator Teller Voss to head its streamlined Industrial Machines division as CEO Dahlia Renn moves to stabilize costs after last quarter's loss. The house said the reorganization consolidates three facilities into two and targets $40M in annualized savings by year-end. Renn told staff the 'hardest cuts are now behind us,' framing the shift as the pivot from teardown to rebuild.

events.head: Carrowforge Returns to Profit as Renn's Post-Split Machines Unit Steadies
events.body: Carrowforge swung back to a $31M quarterly profit from a prior loss, as newly appointed Machines Chief Tobias Kade trimmed overlapping product lines and cut lead times by 18%. CEO Dahlia Renn called the quarter 'proof the split was worth the pain,' though she cautioned that legacy Roe-era divestitures remain incomplete. Order intake for industrial presses rose 12% sequentially.

events.head: Carrowforge Lands $940M Heavy-Press Order as Renn Bets Split Frees Capacity
events.body: Carrowforge secured a $940 million multi-year contract to supply forming presses to a continental fabrication group, its largest single order since the Roe-era split. Machines Chief Owen Talbourne said the deal locks the unit's flagship line at full utilization through 2028. CEO Dahlia Renn called it proof that the leaner post-split structure can win work the old combined house couldn't service.

events.head: Carrowforge Breaks Ground on Second Heavy-Press Line to Fill $940M Order Book
events.body: Renn committed $310M to a new press bay at the flagship works, targeting first output within fourteen months to absorb the record heavy-press backlog. Machines chief Garrick Vale said the expansion adds roughly 40% forming capacity, though Renn acknowledged the timeline leaves 'no margin for slippage.' The move doubles down on the post-split thesis that a leaner Carrowforge can outpace legacy rivals on turnaround time.

events.head: Carrowforge Faces Safety Review After Heavy-Press Weld Fault Surfaces at New Line
events.body: Regulators opened an inspection into Carrowforge's second heavy-press line after workers flagged inconsistent weld seams on three initial frames, halting output for at least two weeks. CEO Dahlia Renn insisted the fault is 'isolated to early tooling calibration' and pledged full cooperation, though the pause threatens delivery timing on the $940M order book. Analysts warn any delay could pressure the freshly restored profit margin.

personality.trait: steady, with the occasional bold move

events.head: Carrowwell — The factory floor's favorite
events.body: Carrowwell is industry talking to industry. Their catalog runs from auto parts and hardware to full industrial machines and material-handling rigs, the kind of iron that earns its keep on a three-shift schedule. Budget lines keep small shops moving; premium machinery anchors the big plants. Maintenance crews stockpile the spares because nothing kills a line like waiting on a part. Solid, unsentimental, and rarely the reason a job runs late.

events.head: Carrowwell Posts Record Quarter as Material Handling Orders Surge
events.body: CEO Theo Thorne reported revenue of $1.4 billion, up 11% year over year, driven by strong demand for conveyor and lift systems amid rival Carrowforge's troubles. The auto parts division also rebounded after a soft prior quarter. Thorne announced a modest capacity boost at two plants to meet the inflow.

events.head: Carrowwell Breaks Ground on New Material Handling Plant
events.body: Riding last quarter's record orders, Carrowwell unveiled plans for a 600,000-square-foot assembly plant in the Eastmere industrial corridor, expected to add 1,400 jobs by 2028. CEO Theo Thorne framed the move as a measured response to surging conveyor and lift demand rather than a gamble, noting the facility is already 40% pre-booked. Construction begins next quarter.

events.head: Carrowwell Unveils Modular Warehouse Automation Line at New Material Handling Plant
events.body: Carrowwell debuted its Meridian modular conveyor and sortation system, the first product built at its newly opened material handling plant. CEO Theo Thorne said the line lets warehouses scale throughput in configurable blocks, targeting mid-size operators priced out of custom installs. Early orders from two regional distributors have already booked out first-quarter capacity.

events.head: Carrowwell Wins Fleet Order for Modular Warehouse Automation Line
events.body: Carrowwell secured a 380 million order to outfit a national distribution operator's facilities with its newly launched modular automation systems. CEO Theo Thorne said the win validates the product bet made at the new material-handling plant, with deliveries beginning next quarter. The contract carries options that could extend its value over three years.

events.head: Carrowwell Lifts Full-Year Outlook as Automation Backlog Swells
events.body: Carrowwell beat estimates with quarterly revenue of 512 million marks, driven by the fleet order for its modular warehouse automation line and firm demand across auto parts. CEO Theo Thorne raised the full-year outlook, citing an automation backlog now stretching past 14 months. The Material Handling segment posted its strongest quarter since the new plant opened.

events.head: Carrowwell Adds Third Shift and Expands Automation Plant to Clear Backlog
events.body: Facing a swelling order book, Carrowwell will add a third production shift and a 90,000-square-foot annex to its Material Handling plant, a roughly $140M commitment. CEO Theo Thorne said the expansion targets an 18-month backlog on the modular warehouse automation line. Hiring for some 320 plant roles begins next quarter.

events.head: Carrowwell Signs $1.1-Billion Multi-Year Automation Pact With National Logistics Network
events.body: Carrowwell secured its largest-ever contract, a $1.1-billion agreement to supply modular warehouse automation across 40 logistics sites over four years. CEO Theo Thorne said the deal transforms the automation unit from a growth line into the company's anchor business. The recently expanded plant and new third shift will be dedicated primarily to fulfilling the rollout.

events.head: Carrowwell Beats and Raises Again as Logistics Automation Pact Kicks In
events.body: Carrowwell reported revenue of $1.42 billion, up 11% year over year, with early deliveries under its $1.1 billion National Logistics Network pact driving the beat. CEO Theo Thorne lifted full-year guidance for the second consecutive quarter and said the backlog now stretches 14 months. Third-shift output has cleared roughly 60% of the prior order overhang.

events.head: Carrowwell Wins $2.4-Billion Industrial Machines Contract to Reindustrialize Aging Plants
events.body: In its largest deal ever, Carrowwell signed a multi-year agreement to supply Industrial Machines and Material Handling systems across a national manufacturing modernization program. CEO Theo Thorne, marking his ninth decade at the helm, called it 'a generational order,' with deliveries phased over five years and expected to add roughly 1,800 jobs.

events.head: Carrowwell Smashes Estimates as Twin Multibillion-Dollar Contracts Fuel Record Quarter
events.body: Theo Thorne delivered a record quarter, with revenue up 24% as the $1.1 billion automation pact and $2.4 billion industrial machines contract both ran at full stride. Order backlog swelled to an all-time high of $8.9 billion, and Carrowwell raised full-year guidance for the third straight period. Thorne said the reindustrialization wave is now Carrowwell's dominant growth engine.

events.head: Carrowwell's Theo Thorne to Retire After Record Run; Mara Voss Named CEO
events.body: Carrowwell announced that Theo Thorne, chief executive since 1934, will step down at year-end following back-to-back record quarters fueled by twin multibillion-dollar contracts. The board named operations chief Mara Voss as successor, tasking her with executing the $2.4B industrial-machines backlog and the logistics automation pact. Thorne will remain as non-executive chairman through the transition.

events.head: Carrowwell Opens Dedicated Machines Plant to Deliver $2.4B Reindustrialization Contract
events.body: In her first major move as CEO, Mara Voss inaugurated a purpose-built industrial machines facility to fulfill the $2.4B plant-modernization contract. The site will handle assembly and final testing, with first deliveries slated for next quarter. Voss framed the plant as proof the company can execute at scale beyond the record run left by predecessor Theo Thorne.

events.head: Carrowwell Unveils Automated Material-Handling System at New Machines Plant
events.body: Carrowwell introduced the Haldon-series material-handling system, its first major product developed at the dedicated machines plant opened to serve its $2.4B reindustrialization contract. CEO Mara Voss said the line targets warehouse and port operators, calling it 'a deliberate push into recurring equipment revenue beyond one-off contracts.'

events.head: Carrowwell Lands $1.1B Follow-On to Extend Reindustrialization Machines Contract
events.body: The new Machines plant secured a $1.1B follow-on award to supply a second phase of the national reindustrialization program, lifting the plant's committed order book past $3.5B. CEO Mara Voss said the automated material-handling system rolled out last quarter cut delivery lead times by 22%, which she credited for winning the extension. Management now expects the plant to reach full capacity a full quarter ahead of schedule.

events.head: Carrowwell Beats as $1.1B Follow-On and New Plant Drive Record Machines Output
events.body: Carrowwell posted quarterly revenue of $1.9B, up 24%, as the dedicated machines plant ramped to full capacity against the extended reindustrialization contract. CEO Mara Voss highlighted early traction for the automated material-handling system, which secured its first external orders outside the government program. The company lifted its backlog figure to $4.6B and reaffirmed margin targets.

events.head: Carrowwell Breaks Ground on Second Machines Plant to Meet $1.1B Contract
events.body: Carrowwell committed $520M to a second industrial-machines facility to serve the extended $1.1B reindustrialization contract, with output slated for late next year. CEO Mara Voss said the plant will also house expanded material-handling assembly following strong reception of the automated system launched this year. The company expects the site to add about 450 skilled positions.

events.head: Carrowwell Beats Again as Second Machines Plant Nears Startup
events.body: Carrowwell posted record quarterly machines output and revenue of $1.4 billion, topping estimates as the $1.1B reindustrialization contract ramped. CEO Mara Voss said the second plant remains on schedule to begin production next quarter, adding capacity for the extended order book.

events.head: Carrowwell Debuts Automated Material-Handling Line as Second Machines Plant Comes Online
events.body: With its second plant now running, Mara Voss introduced a new automated material-handling series aimed at warehouse and logistics buyers, diversifying beyond the $1.1B machines contract. The line launches with two anchor customers and a stated goal of $300M in first-year bookings. Voss said the move hedges Carrowwell's revenue against single-contract concentration.

events.head: Carrowwell Beats as Second Machines Plant Ramps Toward Full Output
events.body: Carrowwell reported earnings of $1.42 per share against expectations near $1.28, with the second Machines plant now running at roughly 70% of capacity against its $1.1B contract. Mara Voss said the automated material-handling line has already booked follow-on orders worth $180M. The company modestly raised its full-year outlook, citing steady demand across its four product lines.

events.head: Carrowwell Edges Past Estimates as Second Machines Plant Reaches Full Output
events.body: Mara Voss reported a narrow beat as the second machines plant hit full production, lifting group revenue 9% on the quarter. Automated material-handling orders continued to build, though Voss flagged softening in auto parts demand as a watch item. Guidance for the year was left unchanged.

events.head: Castle Devices — Sterile, reliable, ready every time
events.body: Castle Devices makes the unglamorous essentials a ward burns through by the hour: syringes, gloves, dressings, tubing, and test kits. Their value range keeps stockrooms full on tight budgets; the mid tier meets the exacting standards of busy surgical floors. Each item is sealed, single-use, and faultless, because in their world a flaw is unthinkable. Nurses reach for Castle without a second glance. The consumables nobody celebrates and no one can do without.

events.head: Castle Devices Renews Long-Term Supply Pact With National Clinic Group
events.body: CEO Bram Calder confirmed a five-year extension to supply sterile consumables to the Brightwell clinic network, valued at roughly $96 million. The renewal preserves the firm's largest recurring revenue stream with no change in pricing. Calder described it as 'business as usual, which is exactly the point.'

events.head: Castle Devices Expands National Clinic Pact to Cover Surgical Consumables
events.body: Castle Devices broadened its long-term supply pact with the National Clinic Group to include a new surgical consumables category, adding an estimated 120 million in annual volume. CEO Bram Calder called the expansion 'a natural next step for a partner that already trusts our shipments,' emphasizing continuity of the existing terms.

events.head: Castle Devices Posts Steady Quarter on Expanded Clinic Volumes
events.body: The medical supplier reported revenue of $612M, up 6% year over year, driven by the broadened surgical consumables pact with National Clinic Group. Bram Calder credited 'orders arriving on time, every time,' with margins holding flat as expected. The results extended Castle's long record of unremarkable but dependable growth.

events.head: Castle Devices Wins Regional Hospital Network Supply Contract
events.body: Calder secured a five-year consumables agreement with the Merrick Regional Hospital Network valued at roughly 380 million marks. The deal broadens Castle's base beyond the National Clinic Group pact and covers both standard and surgical consumables. Calder called it 'steady, predictable work — exactly what we're built for.'

events.head: Castle Devices Posts Steady Quarter as Hospital Network Volumes Kick In
events.body: Castle Devices reported in-line-to-slightly-ahead results, with revenue up 8% as the recently won regional hospital network contract began contributing consumable volumes. CEO Bram Calder pointed to consistent reorder patterns across surgical and general lines. The company held its full-year guidance unchanged.

events.head: Castle Devices Delivers Another Steady Quarter on Consumables Demand
events.body: Castle reported earnings of 1.14 per share, edging past forecasts, as hospital-network consumable volumes held firm and clinic reorders rose 6%. CEO Bram Calder reaffirmed full-year guidance, citing 'no surprises' across the supply base. Margins were flat at 19%.

events.head: Castle Devices Posts Steady Quarter as Consumables Volumes Hold
events.body: Castle Devices reported revenue of $840 million, modestly above estimates, as its regional hospital network contract continued to ramp. Bram Calder reaffirmed full-year guidance and noted consumables reorder rates remained 'reassuringly flat,' consistent with the company's understated cadence.

events.head: Castle Devices Logs Another Steady Quarter as Consumables Demand Holds
events.body: Castle Devices reported revenue up 4% with margins flat, extending its long run of predictable results on steady hospital consumables volumes. CEO Bram Calder reaffirmed guidance and noted a modest expansion of the distribution network in two new regions. Free cash flow again covered the dividend comfortably.

events.head: Castle Devices Logs Yet Another Steady Quarter on Consumables Demand
events.body: Castle Devices reported revenue of $520M, in line with expectations, as consumables volumes held firm across hospital and clinic channels. Bram Calder pointed to renewed multi-year supply agreements as the backbone of the quarter's stability. The company left guidance unchanged for the fourth straight period.

events.head: Castle Devices Marks Another Steady Quarter as Consumables Volumes Hold Firm
events.body: Bram Calder posted broadly flat results in line with expectations, with Medical Consumables shipments holding across hospital and clinic channels. Operating margin held at 19 percent for the fourth straight period. Calder reiterated the house's focus on reliable supply over expansion.

events.head: Castlegear Group — Precision where it matters most
events.body: Castlegear Group equips the rooms where mistakes are measured in lives, supplying medical consumables and equipment across every tier from ward basics to top-end surgical instruments. The luxury line is the standard against which others quietly benchmark themselves. Sterile, exact, and obsessively documented, their kit shows up wherever care cannot be compromised. Clinicians trust the labels without a second glance, which is the highest compliment the field offers.

events.head: Castlegear Group Introduces Refined Surgical Instrument Tray System
events.body: CEO Sable Brandt unveiled an updated modular tray line designed to cut sterilization cycle times for hospital operating rooms. The launch was deliberately limited to three pilot facilities for evaluation before broader rollout. Brandt emphasized the company's preference for 'proving it quietly before promising it loudly.'

events.head: Castlegear Group Wins Multi-Hospital Supply Pact for Tray System
events.body: Sable Brandt secured a five-year agreement to supply its new surgical instrument tray system across the 22-hospital Ellendale Health network. The contract, valued near 118 million, includes consumables replenishment and staff training. Brandt called it 'a measured step that plays to our strengths,' with rollout beginning at flagship facilities this quarter.

events.head: Castlegear Group Adds Equipment Order to Multi-Hospital Tray Pact
events.body: Castlegear expanded its hospital supply relationship with an order for sterilization and instrument-handling equipment valued near $340M over five years. Sable Brandt said the follow-on validates the tray system rollout and deepens ties with the same hospital network group. Deliveries begin next quarter.

events.head: Castlegear Group Tops Estimates as Tray System and Equipment Orders Convert to Revenue
events.body: Castlegear posted revenue of 1.1B, up 6% year on year, as the multi-hospital tray pact and its equipment addendum began shipping in volume. CEO Sable Brandt highlighted a 92% reorder rate on consumables tied to the tray system, calling the recurring stream 'the foundation of steady growth.' The medical supplier reaffirmed its full-year outlook.

events.head: Castlegear Group Edges Ahead as Tray and Equipment Backlog Converts
events.body: Castlegear reported a modest beat, with revenue up 5% as remaining tray-system and equipment orders shipped to hospital partners. CEO Sable Brandt kept guidance unchanged, citing steady reorder patterns and no new large pacts in the pipeline. Management emphasized disciplined cost control over expansion.

events.head: Castlegear Group Wins Regional Network Supply Contract for Sterile Trays
events.body: Castlegear secured a five-year supply agreement with the Merrowfield hospital network valued at roughly $310M, covering sterile tray systems and select equipment servicing. CEO Sable Brandt said the deal extends the company's steady backlog conversion without straining production. Deliveries are scheduled to begin next quarter.

events.head: Castlegear Group Nudges Past Estimates as Regional Trays Contract Ramps
events.body: Sable Brandt posted a modest beat with revenue of $418 million as the regional network sterile-tray contract began contributing meaningfully. Equipment orders held steady, and Brandt reaffirmed a cautious outlook while noting a healthy consumables backlog. The quarter marks a fourth consecutive period of measured growth.

events.head: Castlegear Group Inches Ahead as Sterile Tray Contract Reaches Full Volume
events.body: Castlegear delivered a small beat with income up 4%, as the regional network supply contract for sterile trays reached full shipment volume ahead of schedule. CEO Sable Brandt credited disciplined capacity planning and steady equipment backlog conversion. The company reaffirmed its conservative full-year outlook.

events.head: Castlegear Group Edges Past Estimates as Consumables Volume Holds Steady
events.body: Castlegear reported a modest beat, with sterile tray and consumables volumes holding at full contract levels and quarterly revenue of $288M. Sable Brandt reaffirmed the company's conservative outlook, citing stable demand across its regional network. Margins were unchanged at 16%.

events.head: Castlegear Group Tops Estimates Again as Sterile Tray and Consumables Demand Steadies
events.body: Castlegear Group posted another modest beat as sterile tray shipments held at full volume and consumables demand stayed resilient, lifting revenue 4%. Sable Brandt cited disciplined cost control and reliable regional contracts as the durable core of results. The company reaffirmed its steady full-year outlook.

events.head: Regulators Open Formal Safety Probe Into Castlehold's Saltmere Storage Sites
events.body: A national energy regulator opened a formal investigation Friday into containment failures at Castlehold's Saltmere legacy storage facilities, escalating a crisis that has already produced a $1.9 billion cleanup bill and an investor suit. Ivo Reneth said the company is 'fully cooperating' but declined to estimate potential penalties. Two Saltmere sites were ordered offline pending inspection.

events.head: Castlehold Slashes Guidance as Saltmere Bill Tops $3.1B and Regulators Weigh Site Shutdowns
events.body: Castlehold reported a wider-than-expected quarterly loss and cut full-year guidance after Saltmere cleanup and liability provisions ballooned to $3.1B. The ongoing safety probe now includes a possible suspension order on two of the four Saltmere storage sites, which together hold nearly 40% of the company's capacity. CEO Ivo Reneth acknowledged the firm is exploring asset sales to shore up its balance sheet.

events.head: Castlehold Shuts Three Saltmere Sites and Splits Off Storage Unit as Cleanup Tops $4B
events.body: Under mounting regulatory pressure, Castlehold agreed to permanently close three Saltmere storage sites and carve its remaining storage assets into a separate entity, with total cleanup liabilities now estimated at $4.2 billion. CEO Ivo Reneth framed the move as 'ring-fencing the damage,' but the restructuring wipes out roughly a third of the company's storage capacity and triggers a $900 million writedown.

events.head: Castlehold Faces Class Action Over Saltmere Cleanup as Costs Approach $4.5B
events.body: A coalition of Saltmere-area claimants filed a class-action suit against Castlehold seeking damages tied to the shuttered storage sites, pushing total estimated exposure toward $4.5 billion. CEO Ivo Reneth said the newly separated storage unit is 'ring-fenced' to absorb the liabilities and vowed to contest the broadest claims. Regulators continue to monitor remediation at the three closed facilities.

events.head: Castlehold in Crisis as Leaked Saltmere Files Show Executives Knew of Leaks for Years
events.body: Internal correspondence surfaced showing Castlehold managers documented containment failures at the Saltmere sites as far back as 2022, years before disclosure, sending the cleanup exposure past $5.2B. Ivo Reneth faces mounting calls to resign as the class action expands and two regulators open coordinated inquiries into the withheld records. The company suspended two senior operations officers pending an internal review.

events.head: Castlehold's Reneth Ousted as Board Installs Turnaround Chief Amid Saltmere Fallout
events.body: The board removed Ivo Reneth after mounting pressure over the Saltmere disclosures, naming veteran restructuring executive Halden Voss as chief executive with a mandate to steady finances and settle litigation. Voss inherits cleanup and legal exposure now estimated near $5.2 billion, and pledged a full governance review within 90 days. Shares had lost more than half their value since the leaked files surfaced.

events.head: Castlehold Unveils Sweeping Restructure as Turnaround Chief Carves Out Saltmere Liabilities
events.body: New chief Halden Voss announced plans to ring-fence Saltmere cleanup obligations into a separate managed unit while cutting 1,400 roles and shelving two storage projects to preserve cash. The board approved a $2.1B provision against the class action, and Voss pledged a leaner Power & Storage division focused on 'operable, defensible assets.' Analysts called the plan credible but warned execution risk remains high.

events.head: Castlehold Faces $4.1B Regulator Suit as Saltmere Cleanup Costs Balloon
events.body: State environmental authorities filed a $4.1B civil action against Castlehold, alleging the company concealed groundwater contamination at the Saltmere storage complex for over six years. Turnaround chief Dell Karsh said the carved-out liability unit will absorb the legal exposure, but CEO Halden Voss conceded remediation estimates have nearly doubled to $1.8B. Shares came under fresh pressure as the board disclosed a possible dividend suspension.

events.head: Castlehold Spins Off Saltmere Cleanup Unit as Voss Draws Line Under Legacy Liabilities
events.body: Turnaround chief Halden Voss confirmed the carved-out Saltmere assets will now sit inside a standalone remediation subsidiary, Meridale Environmental, ringfenced with a $1.6B provision. Voss told staff the move lets the core Power & Storage business 'operate without the Saltmere shadow' while the $4.1B regulator suit proceeds separately. Analysts noted the structure caps downside for the parent but leaves cleanup timelines uncertain.

events.head: Castlehold Posts First Clean Quarter Since Saltmere Spin-Off as Voss Turnaround Takes Hold
events.body: Freed of the ring-fenced cleanup unit, Castlehold reported operating profit of $620M against forecasts near $450M, its first result unencumbered by Saltmere provisions. CEO Halden Voss called it 'proof the core business was always sound,' though the $4.1B regulator suit tied to legacy costs remains unresolved.

events.head: Castlehold Wins Landmark Grid-Storage Contract as Voss Turnaround Gains Credibility
events.body: Halden Voss secured a $780M Power & Storage supply deal to anchor the Ardent regional grid, the group's largest since the Saltmere spin-off. The multi-year agreement locks in baseline revenue and validates Voss's push to reposition Castlehold around clean capacity. Management said the contract covers roughly a third of planned storage output through 2029.

events.head: Castlehold Unveils Modular Storage Platform as Voss Builds on Grid Momentum
events.body: Castlehold introduced its Halden-branded Meridian storage system, a stackable battery unit targeting utility clients who signed on after last quarter's grid-storage win. Voss said early orders cover roughly 1.2 gigawatt-hours of capacity, with first deliveries slated for the fourth quarter. Management framed the launch as proof the turnaround has shifted from cleanup to growth.

events.head: Castlehold Breaks Ground on Second Plant to Scale Modular Storage Platform
events.body: Castlehold committed roughly $310 million to a second production facility dedicated to its recently launched modular storage platform, aiming to double capacity by late 2027. CEO Halden Voss framed the build as necessary to meet demand from the landmark grid-storage contract. The move marks Castlehold's first greenfield expansion since the Saltmere spin-off.

events.head: Castlehold Rolls Out High-Capacity Modular Line as Second Plant Nears Completion
events.body: Halden Voss unveiled the next tier of the modular storage platform, doubling per-unit capacity and targeting large grid operators. The launch coincides with the second plant reaching 80% construction, positioning Castlehold to begin shipments by mid-year. Voss said early letters of intent already cover roughly 40% of the plant's projected first-year output.

events.head: Castlehold Wins $750M Supply Deal for High-Capacity Modular Storage
events.body: Castlehold secured a $750M multi-year supply agreement to deliver its new high-capacity modular line to a regional grid operator, its largest order to date. CEO Halden Voss said the second plant's completion would be timed to first deliveries, though he acknowledged execution risk in the compressed schedule. The deal validates the platform Voss has raced to scale since taking the helm.

events.head: Castlehold Beats as $750M Supply Deal Ships First Modular Units
events.body: Castlehold posted quarterly revenue of $412M, up 34% year-on-year, as initial deliveries under its $750M storage supply agreement began flowing from the completed second plant. CEO Halden Voss credited the high-capacity modular line for lifting gross margins to 28%, though he cautioned that ramp costs would weigh on the coming quarter. The company reaffirmed full-year output targets.

events.head: Castlehold Fires Up Second Plant as Modular Backlog Swells to $1.2B
events.body: Castlehold formally opened its second manufacturing plant, roughly doubling capacity for its high-capacity modular storage line as the order backlog climbed to $1.2B. CEO Halden Voss said the facility will reach full output within two quarters and hire some 400 workers. Voss acknowledged the aggressive ramp carries execution risk but insisted demand 'leaves us no choice but to move fast.'

events.head: Castlehold Lands Landmark $2B Grid-Storage Framework, Its Largest Ever
events.body: Halden Voss secured a multi-year framework worth up to $2B to supply high-capacity modular storage to a consortium of regional utilities, more than doubling the firm's existing backlog to over $3B. Deliveries begin next quarter and will require Castlehold to accelerate a planned third plant. The deal cements Voss's aggressive first-year expansion, though it also raises execution risk given how fast the order book has swelled.

events.head: Castlehold Smashes Estimates as $2B Framework and Twin Plants Drive Record Quarter
events.body: Castlehold reported record revenue of $980M, up 62%, as its landmark $2B grid-storage framework began delivering and both modular plants ran near capacity. Halden Voss said backlog now exceeds $2.8B and hinted at a third facility to keep pace. Net income tripled to $166M, though Voss cautioned that scaling this fast carries execution risk.

events.head: Castlehold Faces Regulatory Probe After Grid-Storage Incident at Second Plant
events.body: Regulators opened a formal safety investigation into Castlehold following a thermal event at its newly commissioned second plant that forced a temporary shutdown of one storage array. No injuries were reported, but the probe casts a shadow over the $2B grid-storage framework and the aggressive dual-plant expansion driven by CEO Halden Voss. The company said it is cooperating fully and has paused new array energization pending review.

events.head: Castlehold Ordered to Halt Second Plant as Probe Escalates and Framework Delivery Slips
events.body: Regulators widened their investigation into Castlehold's grid-storage incident, ordering a full shutdown of the second plant pending a design review and citing 'systemic containment concerns.' The halt jeopardizes near-term deliveries under the company's flagship $2B framework, and CEO Halden Voss acknowledged 'material schedule risk' while insisting the underlying technology is sound. Two customers have requested contract reviews.

events.head: Castlehold Slashes Guidance and Books $600M Charge as Framework Deal Collapses
events.body: With its second plant still halted under the escalating probe, Castlehold's $2B framework partner exercised exit clauses tied to delivery slippage, forcing Voss to withdraw full-year guidance and record a $600M impairment. The turbulent chief announced a sweeping restructuring including a hiring freeze and the pause of a planned third plant. The reversal erased the record quarter that opened the year and rattled confidence in Voss's aggressive expansion.

events.head: Castlehold Ousts Voss as Board Installs New Chief After Framework Collapse
events.body: Castlehold's board removed CEO Halden Voss following the collapse of the Framework deal, the $600M charge, and the second-plant shutdown, naming turnaround veteran Ingrid Mally as chief executive. Mally said her first priority is resolving the outstanding regulatory probe and stabilizing grid-storage operations before pursuing new mandates. The board also suspended forward guidance pending a strategic review.

events.head: Castlehold's Mally Launches Sweeping Turnaround, Exits Storage-Framework Ambitions
events.body: New chief Ingrid Mally unveiled a 90-day reset plan that shelves the abandoned Framework program entirely and refocuses the company on its core Power & Storage baseload contracts. The plan targets $220M in annual savings and consolidates operations around the two plants cleared by regulators, while the halted second plant remains offline pending final review. Mally called the previous strategy 'overextended' and pledged a return to disciplined delivery.

events.head: Castlestead — Feeds the ground that feeds us
events.body: Born in farm country, Castlestead arms growers with earthmoving gear, farm equipment, and the inputs that turn dirt into a harvest. Smallholders lean on the affordable line; large operations run the premium machines hard through every season. Built to start cold, work wet, and forgive a missed service, their kit treats the calendar as the real boss. Generations of families have planted, plowed, and prospered behind that name.

events.head: Castlestead Unveils Low-Till Seeder Line for Compacted Soils
events.body: Castlestead introduced its new Greenfurrow seeding range, engineered to plant directly into hardened ground without heavy turnover. CEO Aurelia Calder framed the launch as a careful answer to soil-erosion complaints from longtime grower clients, with initial units shipping to regional cooperatives this season.

events.head: Castlestead Wins Multi-Year Supply Deal With Cooperative Harrowfield Growers
events.body: Castlestead signed a four-year agreement to supply farm inputs and low-till seeders to the 1,200-member Harrowfield Growers cooperative. CEO Aurelia Calder said the deal, estimated at $190M, validates the recently launched seeder line and reflects rising demand for equipment suited to compacted soils.

events.head: Castlestead Adds Nutrient-Blend Farm Inputs to Pair With Low-Till Line
events.body: Castlestead introduced a soil-conditioning input blend designed to complement its low-till seeders on compacted ground, rolling out first to Harrowfield cooperative members. Aurelia Calder framed the launch as a measured extension rather than a new bet, with wider availability planned for next season.

events.head: Castlestead Edges Ahead as Low-Till and Nutrient-Blend Lines Pair Up
events.body: Castlestead reported a modest beat with revenue of $890M against $865M expected, helped by attach rates on nutrient blends sold alongside its low-till seeders. CEO Aurelia Calder said the Harrowfield cooperative deal delivered steady early volumes and repeat farm-input orders. Guidance was reaffirmed with a cautious note on planting-season weather.

events.head: Castlestead Posts Quiet Beat as Harrowfield Supply Deal Ramps Up
events.body: Aurelia Calder reported a slim 1.9% revenue gain as first shipments under the Harrowfield Growers agreement flowed alongside steady nutrient-blend sales. The company held its conservative full-year outlook, citing normal seasonal earthmoving softness. Calder made no new commitments, in keeping with her measured approach.

events.head: Castlestead Posts Modest Beat as Harrowfield Deal Reaches Full Volume
events.body: Castlestead edged past expectations as the Harrowfield Supply agreement hit full run-rate, lifting Farm Inputs revenue 8%. CEO Aurelia Calder noted steady demand for the paired low-till and nutrient-blend lines through the planting season. The conservative agriculture house left guidance unchanged and reaffirmed its dividend.

events.head: Castlestead Posts Another Quiet Beat as Harrowfield Deal Steadies
events.body: The agriculture house reported a slim beat with revenue up 3%, as the Harrowfield supply deal held at full volume and low-till equipment sales stayed firm. CEO Aurelia Calder maintained the company's conservative full-year outlook, citing 'no surprises we didn't plan for.' Nutrient-blend lines continued to pair steadily with equipment orders.

events.head: Castlestead Posts Slim Beat as Farm Inputs Offset Softer Earthmoving
events.body: Castlestead edged past estimates as steady Farm Inputs demand cushioned a modest dip in Earthmoving orders. CEO Aurelia Calder characterized the quarter as unremarkable, with the mature Harrowfield deal continuing to bill on schedule. Management reaffirmed its conservative full-year outlook.
