events.body: Korrwright secured a renewal and expansion of its Verant supply arrangement valued near $210M, locking in structural-materials and wire volumes for six additional years. CEO Halden Fenn said the deal underpins utilization at the new wire line and supports a modest dividend lift. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance on the strengthened backlog.

events.head: Korrwright Group Breaks Ground on Structural Materials Plant to Anchor Verant Corridor
events.body: Korrwright committed $340 million to a new Structural Materials facility near the Verant corridor, positioning it to bundle materials with its extended wire contract through 2031. CEO Halden Fenn framed the move as 'meeting Verant where it is heading, not where it stands,' with first output slated for late next year.

events.head: Korrwright Group Opens Verant Corridor Plant, Ships First Structural Beams
events.body: The new Verant Corridor plant rolled out its first structural beam line three weeks ahead of schedule, with initial output earmarked for corridor infrastructure work. Halden Fenn said the facility would reach full capacity of 340,000 tonnes annually by mid-cycle, tightening Korrwright's grip on the region it has supplied wire to since 2028.

events.head: Korrwright Group Wins $1.4B Corridor Infrastructure Package Spanning Beams and Cable
events.body: Halden Fenn secured a $1.4 billion multi-year award to supply structural materials and wire for the next phase of the Verant Corridor buildout. The contract pairs the recently opened corridor plant with Korrwright's cable operations, locking in demand through 2032. Fenn called it validation of the vertically integrated bet the company placed on the corridor.

events.head: Korrwright Group Beats as Corridor Package Drives Record Beam and Cable Shipments
events.body: Korrwright Group posted revenue of $2.1 billion, up 19%, as the $1.4B corridor infrastructure package entered peak delivery across beams and wire. CEO Halden Fenn said the Verant Corridor plant is running at 85% capacity less than a year after opening. Backlog stood at $3.6 billion, giving the company visibility into 2027.

events.head: Korrwright Group Adds Second Line at Verant Corridor Plant to Clear Backlog
events.body: Korrwright approved a $180M second production line at its Verant Corridor plant to keep pace with the $1.4B infrastructure package. CEO Halden Fenn said cable output will roughly double once the line reaches full rate next year, easing lead times that had stretched to record lengths. The expansion adds an estimated 300 jobs at the site.

events.head: Korrwright Group Lands $600M Rail-Bridge Contract to Follow Corridor Work
events.body: Korrwright Group secured a $600 million package to supply structural beams and wire assemblies for a regional rail-bridge program, extending demand well past its current Verant corridor backlog. CEO Halden Fenn said the win validates the decision to add a second line, which will now run near capacity into next year. Deliveries begin in the second half.

events.head: Korrwright Group Beats Again as Rail-Bridge Work Joins Corridor Backlog
events.body: Korrwright reported quarterly revenue of $1.4B, up 11% year over year, as the $600M rail-bridge contract began contributing alongside the ongoing corridor package. CEO Halden Fenn cited the second Verant line for holding delivery times steady despite record combined beam and cable volumes. The order book now stretches nearly two years out.

events.head: Korrwright Group Wins $310M Wire & Cable Supply Award for Corridor Region
events.body: Korrwright Group secured a $310M multi-year contract to supply structural wire and cable for utility upgrades across the Verant Corridor region. CEO Halden Fenn said the win leverages the second line added earlier this year and pairs naturally with the ongoing rail-bridge work. The contract lifts the company's forward backlog to a record level.

events.head: Korrwright Group Beats as Corridor and Rail-Bridge Backlog Both Bill
events.body: Korrwright posted quarterly revenue of $1.14B, up 18% year on year, as its $600M rail-bridge job and the corridor wire-and-cable award began billing in parallel. Halden Fenn pointed to a backlog now exceeding $2.6B, the deepest in the group's recorded history.

events.head: Korrwright Group Secures $420M Structural Materials Award for Harbor Redevelopment
events.body: Korrwright won a $420M contract to supply structural materials for a multi-year harbor redevelopment, extending its backlog well into the decade. CEO Halden Fenn said the award pairs naturally with the existing corridor and rail-bridge work, allowing shared logistics and steadier plant utilization. The company now carries one of its largest combined backlogs in recent memory.

events.head: Korrwright Group Beats as Harbor and Corridor Awards Begin Billing
events.body: Korrwright posted a beat on revenue of $1.48B, with the $420M Harbor redevelopment and $310M Corridor wire award both entering the billing cycle. Halden Fenn said combined backlog now stands at a record $2.1B, giving the group visibility deep into next year. Management nudged full-year guidance modestly higher on the strength of the structural segment.

events.head: Korrwright Group Beats as Harbor Redevelopment Enters Peak Billing
events.body: Korrwright Group posted revenue of $1.31B, ahead of estimates, as the $420M Harbor redevelopment award moved into its heaviest structural-materials phase. CEO Halden Fenn said combined harbor and corridor billing lifted Structural Materials volumes to a two-year high, though he flagged tighter input costs on Wire & Cable. Full-year guidance was nudged upward.

events.head: Korrwright Group Edges Past Estimates as Harbor Billing Holds at Peak
events.body: Korrwright reported a narrow beat with revenue of $610M as Harbor redevelopment billing held near its peak and the corridor award continued to ramp. Halden Fenn said structural-materials volumes stayed firm but flagged that Harbor billing would begin tapering next quarter. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance without raising it.

events.head: Korrwright Group Wins $3.4B Transit Corridor Contract in Largest Award in Its History
events.body: Halden Fenn secured the multi-year Eastreach Corridor package, supplying structural materials and wire & cable for a regional rail and utility spine. The award, worth $3.4B over six years, arrives just as Harbor redevelopment billing peaks, giving Korrwright a rare double-anchor backlog. Fenn said the win 'extends visibility well into the next decade' and lifts total backlog past $9B.

events.head: Korrwright Works Unveils First Timepieces Built on In-House Vellhorn Escapements
events.body: Korrwright debuted its Meridian collection, the first line to feature escapements from the recently acquired Vellhorn Movements, priced from $8,400. CEO Dunmore Carrow said full vertical integration cuts reliance on outside suppliers and improves margins on the heritage division's flagship pieces. Initial allocations to boutiques are already spoken for.

events.head: Korrwright Works Seals $1.2B Takeover of Heritage Rival Ambrose & Sons
events.body: In his boldest move in decades, Dunmore Carrow has agreed to acquire storied competitor Ambrose & Sons for $1.2 billion, folding its two-century dial-making workshops and prestige boutiques into the Korrwright stable. The deal doubles Korrwright's atelier capacity and adds the coveted Ambrose Meridian collection, though analysts note Carrow now faces the challenge of integrating three heritage brands at once. Regulators in two markets are expected to review the combination over the coming months.

events.head: Korrwright Works Folds Ambrose & Sons Into New Heritage Division
events.body: Following its $1.2B takeover, Korrwright Works announced it will consolidate Ambrose & Sons and the acquired Vellhorn movements arm under a single Heritage Division led from the Carrow flagship workshop. CEO Dunmore Carrow said the reorganization will trim roughly 260 overlapping roles while preserving Ambrose's landmark casing atelier. The firm expects $90M in annual cost savings from combined escapement production by the second year.

events.head: Korrwright Works Beats as Heritage Division Lifts Margins
events.body: Korrwright reported a 14% revenue rise, with the newly folded Ambrose & Sons operations contributing ahead of internal targets in their first full quarter. CEO Dunmore Carrow credited shared Vellhorn escapement tooling for cutting per-unit costs across both brands. Management hinted that integration savings would free capital for further acquisitions.

events.head: Korrwright Works Opens Flagship Heritage Atelier as Carrow Eyes New Markets
events.body: Dunmore Carrow cut the ribbon on a restored downtown atelier that consolidates Korrwright and Ambrose & Sons craftsmanship under one roof, adding roughly 120 master watchmakers. The 40,000-square-foot facility is expected to lift annual output of high-complication timepieces by nearly a third. Carrow hinted the site is a launchpad for entry into two overseas luxury markets next year.

events.head: Korrwright Works Seizes Rival Meridienne in $2.4B Cross-Border Coup
events.body: Dunmore Carrow moved on longtime competitor Meridienne Horlogerie, acquiring the storied movement-house for $2.4 billion in the largest deal of his 118-year tenure. The purchase hands the new Heritage Division control of Meridienne's celebrated tourbillon workshops and opens the eastern markets Carrow had publicly targeted. Executives said Meridienne's 340 master watchmakers will be retained under the Korrwright banner.

events.head: Korrwright Works Folds Meridienne Into New 'Korrwright Meridienne' Luxury House
events.body: Korrwright Works unveiled a unified luxury identity, rebranding its acquired rival under the combined 'Korrwright Meridienne' banner to consolidate heritage collections under one crest. CEO Dunmore Carrow said the merged house would share ateliers while preserving Meridienne's signature movements. Management expects the rebrand to lift blended margins as duplicate distribution costs are stripped out.

events.head: Korrwright Works Slips as Meridienne Integration Costs Bite
events.body: Quarterly earnings came in 11% below expectations as the $2.4B Meridienne acquisition dragged margins with duplicated overhead and rebranding spend. Dunmore Carrow acknowledged 'a heavier lift than modeled' but insisted the combined Korrwright Meridienne house would deliver by next fiscal year. Integration charges totaled $310M, the bulk tied to consolidating two overlapping atelier networks.

events.head: Korrwright Works Reopens Meridienne Salon in Grand Relaunch as Integration Costs Ease
events.body: With the worst of the merger charges behind it, Korrwright Works has poured $180M into refurbishing the flagship Korrwright Meridienne salon, restoring the acquired workshops to full craft capacity. CEO Dunmore Carrow framed the relaunch as 'the payoff phase,' telling reporters the combined house now spans two centuries of horological heritage under one roof.

events.head: Korrwright Works Beats as Reopened Meridienne Salon Drives Luxury Demand
events.body: Quarterly revenue rose 11% to $482M as the relaunched Meridienne salon posted record footfall and higher average ticket prices on limited-run timepieces. Dunmore Carrow credited the integration for lifting group margins back above 28%, reversing the prior quarter's slip. The house said waitlists for its flagship complications now stretch into next year.

events.head: Korrwright Works Acquires Heritage Movement Maker Alvence in $340M Deal
events.body: Korrwright Works has agreed to buy movement specialist Alvence for $340 million, extending CEO Dunmore Carrow's acquisitive streak on the back of the Meridienne salon's revival. The purchase secures in-house mechanical calibers that had previously been sourced externally, echoing rivals' move toward vertical integration. Carrow said Alvence's workshops will supply the reopened Meridienne line first.

events.head: Korrwright Works Debuts Alvence-Built In-House Movement in Meridienne Flagship
events.body: Five months after the $340M Alvence acquisition, Korrwright unveiled the Meridienne Calibre 12, its first timepiece using a fully in-house movement from the Alvence workshops. CEO Dunmore Carrow priced the debut edition at $58,000 and capped the first run at 400 pieces, saying vertical control of movements ends the house's reliance on outside suppliers. Early salon allocations reportedly cleared within days of the private preview.

events.head: Korrwright Works Beats as In-House Alvence Movement Lifts Margins
events.body: Korrwright posted quarterly revenue up 18% with gross margin widening nearly three points, which management credited to bringing Alvence movement production in-house. CEO Dunmore Carrow said the Meridienne flagship's in-house calibre line has outpaced supply since debut, prompting a waitlist at the salon. The company reaffirmed plans to migrate more collections onto Alvence movements.

events.head: Korrwright Works Acquires Retail Chain Verenne in $780M Bid to Control Distribution
events.body: In its boldest move yet, CEO Dunmore Carrow struck an $780M deal to buy the 44-boutique Verenne retail network, giving Korrwright direct shelf presence across premium markets for the first time. The acquisition marks a shift from Carrow's movement-maker buying spree toward controlling how Meridienne flagships reach buyers. Analysts note the deal roughly doubles Korrwright's retail footprint and layers integration risk onto an already busy balance sheet.

events.head: Korrwright Works Folds Verenne Into New Retail Division as Integration Begins
events.body: Korrwright unveiled a reorganization creating a dedicated retail arm to absorb the $780M Verenne chain, consolidating boutiques under a single Meridienne-branded storefront strategy. CEO Dunmore Carrow said the move eliminates roughly 40 overlapping locations while adding flagship space in three new markets. Integration costs will weigh on next-quarter margins.

events.head: Korrwright Works Beats as Verenne Retail Integration Lifts Direct Sales
events.body: Korrwright Works reported a 22% revenue rise to $610M in its first full quarter with the Verenne retail division consolidated, as direct-to-boutique sales of Alvence-movement pieces expanded margins to 41%. CEO Dunmore Carrow said controlling distribution has already trimmed discounting and improved inventory turns. He signaled appetite for further boutique acquisitions in key luxury corridors.

events.head: Korrwright Works Strikes $1.1B Deal for Movement-Maker Halbrook in Vertical Leap
events.body: Korrwright Works agreed to acquire in-house movement specialist Halbrook Manufacture for $1.1B, its largest deal ever, securing control of a critical supply link long outsourced. CEO Dunmore Carrow said pairing Halbrook's movements with the Verenne retail network gives Korrwright end-to-end command 'from bench to boutique.' The purchase, expected to close next quarter, adds roughly 1,300 workers and two workshops to the house.

events.head: Korrwright Works Debuts In-House Escapement as Halbrook Integration Bears Fruit
events.body: Six months after the $1.1B Halbrook acquisition, Korrwright unveiled its first fully in-house escapement mechanism, ending decades of reliance on outside movement suppliers. Carrow told assembled press the milestone 'closes the last open link in our chain,' and hinted that a limited grand-complication series would follow within the year.

events.head: Korrwright Works Wins Grand Prix at Verenne Horology Salon for In-House Escapement
events.body: The reborn escapement, developed after the $1.1B Halbrook acquisition, took top honors at the prestigious Verenne salon, a first for the 118-year-old house. Chief executive Dunmore Carrow said the award validates the vertical-integration strategy and lifts order visibility into next year. The recognition arrives as direct sales from Verenne retail continue to outpace wholesale.

events.head: Korrwright Works Breaks Ground on Halbrook Movement Campus to Triple Escapement Output
events.body: Fresh off its Verenne Grand Prix, Korrwright Works committed $320 million to a new movement campus adjacent to the acquired Halbrook works. CEO Dunmore Carrow said the expansion will triple in-house escapement capacity by 2029 and end reliance on outside suppliers entirely. The facility is expected to add roughly 600 skilled positions at peak.

events.head: Korrwright Works Unveils Halbrook Perpetual, First Complication Built Entirely In-House
events.body: Dunmore Carrow presented the Halbrook Perpetual, a perpetual calendar priced at $148,000 and running on the house's own escapement and movement architecture. The launch marks the first Korrwright complication with zero outsourced components, a milestone Carrow called 'the payoff of the Halbrook campus.' Initial allocation of 220 pieces sold out to authorized salons within days.

events.head: Korrwright Works Takes Complication Prize at Verenne for Halbrook Perpetual
events.body: The Halbrook Perpetual earned the Complication Prize at the Verenne Horology Salon, a second consecutive honor for Korrwright and validation of its fully in-house strategy. CEO Dunmore Carrow said the award confirms the wisdom of the Halbrook Movement Campus buildout now underway. Judges cited the escapement's precision and the achievement of a perpetual calendar built entirely without outside suppliers.

events.head: Korrwright Works Acquires Verenne Case-Maker Dovreux Frères in $620M Deal
events.body: Dunmore Carrow announced the purchase of storied case and dial specialist Dovreux Frères, bringing another rung of the supply chain in-house just months after the Halbrook Perpetual's prize win. The all-cash deal absorbs Dovreux's three ateliers and roughly 480 finishers, and Carrow said its guilloché workshop would supply the entire Halbrook line by next season. Analysts noted it is Korrwright's largest single acquisition in over a decade.

events.head: Korrwright Works Debuts First Timepiece Built on Newly Acquired Dovreux Cases
events.body: Just months after the $620M Dovreux Frères deal, CEO Dunmore Carrow unveiled the Halbrook Meridian, the first Korrwright piece using in-house-controlled Dovreux casework. The limited run of 300 carries a list price near $148,000 and showcases the vertical integration Carrow promised at acquisition. Early allocations to Verenne dealers sold through within days.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Breaks Ground on Fifth Cell-Pack Line as Brandt Chases Scale
events.body: Fresh off absorbing Delphin's plants, Cole Brandt announced a $2.1 billion investment to add a fifth cell-pack line at the newly unified Halbrook complex. The move lifts targeted annual output past 40 gigawatt-hours and, Brandt told reporters, positions Lhaus to underbid rivals on volume contracts. Analysts noted the pace reflects Brandt's long habit of building faster than demand strictly requires.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Misses as Cell-Pack Buildout Costs Squeeze Margins
events.body: Lhaus reported quarterly profit below expectations as the rapid Delphin integration and fifth-line construction pushed capital spending and startup costs higher than guided. Margins in the cell-pack segment slipped to 9.1% from 13.4% a year earlier, though Cole Brandt insisted the scale push would pay off once new lines reach full run-rate. Vehicle and parts units held steady.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Pauses Sixth Cell-Pack Line, Trims Buildout to Protect Margins
events.body: Following last quarter's earnings miss, Lhaus announced it will delay its planned sixth cell-pack line and consolidate two underused Delphin sub-assemblies, targeting $180 million in annualized savings. CEO Cole Brandt said the moves would 'let the existing five lines earn their keep' before further expansion. The company maintained its full-year volume outlook but conceded margin recovery would take two to three quarters.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Returns to a Beat as Trimmed Buildout Restores Margins
events.body: After two rough quarters, Lhaus topped estimates as the paused sixth-line spend fell out of the cost base and the five running cell-pack lines reached target yields. CEO Cole Brandt said free cash flow turned positive again and hinted the sixth line could restart 'once the numbers earn it,' signaling his acquisitive streak isn't fully cooled.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Restarts Sixth Cell-Pack Line as Brandt Eyes Storage Push
events.body: With margins stabilized, CEO Cole Brandt greenlit the resumption of the previously paused sixth cell-pack line, backed by a $420 million capital commitment. Brandt framed the move as a return to offense, targeting a 30% lift in Power & Storage output by next year to chase surging grid-storage demand.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Secures $2.8B Grid-Storage Supply Pact in Landmark Storage Pivot
events.body: Cole Brandt landed a multi-year agreement to supply cell packs for a national grid-storage operator, validating the restarted sixth line and the broader storage push. The deal, worth up to $2.8B over six years, marks Lhaus's largest single contract outside automotive parts. Brandt called it 'the transformation we restarted that line for.'

events.head: Lhaus Industries Breaks Ground on Dedicated Grid-Storage Plant to Serve $2.8B Pact
events.body: Lhaus committed $640 million to a purpose-built cell-pack facility in Vantmoor, its first plant devoted entirely to grid-storage output under the landmark supply pact. Cole Brandt said the site will run four assembly lines at launch with room to double, easing pressure on the six retrofitted automotive lines. Initial deliveries from the plant are targeted within 18 months.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Seals Second Grid-Storage Megadeal Worth $3.4B, Cementing Storage Pivot
events.body: Lhaus stunned the sector by landing a $3.4B, seven-year grid-storage supply agreement with a consortium of utilities, its largest contract ever and second major storage win in under a year. CEO Cole Brandt said the deal validates the pivot away from legacy auto parts and pledged to fast-track a second dedicated storage plant. Combined storage backlog now exceeds $6B.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Faces Regulatory Probe After Grid-Storage Overheating Reports
events.body: Regulators opened a formal safety review into Lhaus Industries' grid-storage units following three reported thermal incidents at customer sites tied to its $2.8 billion pact. The probe casts a shadow over Cole Brandt's aggressive storage pivot, with the second $3.4 billion megadeal now under contractual review. Brandt said the company is 'cooperating fully' and has paused shipments from the new dedicated plant pending inspection.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Recalls Grid-Storage Units Across Two Megadeals as Probe Confirms Overheating Fault
events.body: Lhaus issued a recall covering roughly 60,000 grid-storage modules delivered under its $2.8B and $3.4B pacts after regulators confirmed a thermal-management defect behind earlier overheating reports. Cole Brandt said both anchor buyers were notified and that the dedicated storage plant would shift to a corrected design, at an estimated $320 million cost. The company said it aims to preserve delivery commitments but flagged possible schedule slippage on the second megadeal.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Sued for $1.8B as Grid-Storage Partners Allege Concealed Overheating Data
events.body: Two megadeal counterparties filed a joint $1.8B suit claiming Lhaus withheld internal thermal-test findings before signing the grid-storage contracts. The complaint alleges CEO Cole Brandt's team accelerated deployments despite known fault margins, deepening the fallout from last quarter's recall. Lhaus called the claims 'without merit' but disclosed it has set aside $400M in reserves.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Carves Out Grid-Storage Division Amid Mounting Legal Pressure
events.body: Cole Brandt announced Lhaus will spin its embattled Power & Storage operations into a ring-fenced subsidiary, a move designed to contain liability from the $1.8 billion partner lawsuit. The reorganization includes a $400 million provision for settlements and remediation, alongside leadership changes across the storage unit. Brandt framed the step as protecting the core auto parts and vehicles businesses from further fallout.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Misses as Grid-Storage Carve-Out Costs and Legal Reserves Weigh
events.body: Lhaus Industries missed quarterly forecasts, posting a 14% profit drop as it booked $420M in reserves tied to the $1.8B overheating suit and one-time costs from carving out its grid-storage division. CEO Cole Brandt said the core auto-parts and vehicles units remained solid, but conceded the storage fallout would 'shadow results into next year.' Settlement talks with two former megadeal partners are reportedly underway.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Offloads Carved-Out Grid-Storage Unit to Kessering Group for $900M
events.body: Cole Brandt announced the sale of the ring-fenced grid-storage division to private holding firm Kessering Group for $900 million, transferring the bulk of the overheating litigation exposure with it. Brandt framed the deal as clearing the deck for a renewed push into vehicles and auto parts, calling storage 'a chapter we no longer need.' The buyer assumes the pending $1.8B partner claims as part of the terms.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Redeploys Kessering Proceeds Into $650M Vehicle-Platform Buyout
events.body: Fresh off shedding its grid-storage unit, Cole Brandt moved fast to acquire drivetrain specialist Marnick Motive for $650M, folding it into the core Vehicles arm. Executives said the deal restores the growth narrative after two turbulent quarters and adds three assembly lines. Brandt called it a return to 'what Lhaus was built to do.'

events.head: Lhaus Industries Rolls Out First Vehicle Line Built on Newly Acquired Platform
events.body: Cole Brandt debuted the Verrant midsize range, the first models engineered on the $650M platform Lhaus bought earlier this year, targeting 120,000 units in the first full production year. Brandt framed the launch as proof the acquisition-heavy strategy is bearing fruit, telling reporters the platform will underpin at least four nameplates by 1957. Early dealer commitments cover roughly 40% of planned volume.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Beats as New Platform Vehicle Line Outsells Forecasts
events.body: Cole Brandt reported revenue of $2.4 billion, up 9%, as the first vehicle line built on the acquired platform sold 42,000 units in its opening quarter, beating internal targets by a fifth. The Kessering divestiture proceeds continued to fund a leaner, vehicle-focused footprint. Brandt hinted at 'one or two more bolt-ons' to round out the auto-parts side.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Buys Parts Supplier Verrund for $480M to Deepen Platform Control
events.body: Restless as ever, Cole Brandt struck again, acquiring drivetrain specialist Verrund for $480M to bring key components of its new vehicle platform in-house. The deal is expected to trim per-unit costs by 9% and secure supply as the platform line outsells forecasts. Brandt said vertical integration was 'the natural next move' after the strong launch.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Beats as Verrund Integration Cuts Parts Costs
events.body: Lhaus posted a quarterly beat as the newly acquired Verrund supplier trimmed component costs on its fast-selling platform vehicle line. CEO Cole Brandt credited tighter parts control for a 3-point margin gain and hinted at further supply-chain deals ahead. Vehicle deliveries continued to outpace forecasts.

events.head: Lhaus Industries to Acquire Battery Maker Kellstrom for $2.1B in Push Into Power & Storage
events.body: Cole Brandt unveiled the $2.1B cash-and-stock purchase of Kellstrom, a maker of grid and vehicle storage cells, in the largest deal of his seven-decade run atop Lhaus. The move vertically links Kellstrom's cell output to Lhaus's Power & Storage unit and its platform vehicle line, though it lifts the company's debt load to a decade high. Brandt called storage 'the next platform' and said Kellstrom's two plants would run under Lhaus branding by year-end.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Forms Power & Storage Division Around Newly Acquired Kellstrom
events.body: Cole Brandt confirmed the $2.1B Kellstrom deal has closed and will anchor a standalone Power & Storage division, folding in Lhaus's existing cell operations. The unit targets $1.4B in revenue within three years, with Kellstrom's Renfield plant retooled to supply Lhaus vehicle platforms directly. Brandt named the segment 'the third leg' alongside Auto Parts and Vehicles.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Debuts First Kellstrom-Based Storage Pack Under New Power Division
events.body: Cole Brandt introduced the LX-Cell modular storage unit, the first product to emerge from the Kellstrom integration, targeting fleet depots and small grid installations. Division head Sable Ory said pre-orders cover 60,000 units, with shipments beginning next quarter from the retooled Kellstrom line. Brandt framed the launch as proof the $2.1B acquisition can move beyond parts synergies into standalone revenue.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Wins $4.3B Fleet Storage Contract in Landmark Power Division Deal
events.body: Cole Brandt secured a multi-year agreement to supply Kellstrom-based storage packs to a national logistics fleet operator, the largest single order in the young Power & Storage division's history. The $4.3B contract locks in output through 2032 and validates the $2.1B Kellstrom acquisition Brandt championed. Shares of the vertically integrated automaker reflected the strategic milestone as the division moved from launch to scale.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Beats as Power Division Deliveries Begin Under $4.3B Fleet Deal
events.body: CEO Cole Brandt posted a quarterly profit of $610M, ahead of expectations, as first shipments under the landmark fleet storage contract began recognizing revenue. The Kellstrom-based Power & Storage unit contributed 22% of group sales in its first full quarter. Brandt hinted at further bolt-on acquisitions to feed the fast-growing division.

events.head: Maison & Vale — Order, in every quiet detail
events.body: Maison & Vale brought a touch of grace to the workaday business of keeping house. Their cleaning supplies, janitorial lines, and household goods marry function with a finish you'd actually want on display. The value range earns its place in everyday cupboards; the mid tier dresses boutique stays and well-run homes. There's a pleasing weight to their wares, a sense someone cared. Tidiness raised, gently, to something close to a small pleasure.

events.head: Maison & Vale Acquires Cleaning-Supply Maker Sundle Werks
events.body: The hospitality group has purchased Sundle Werks, a mid-sized jansan manufacturer, for $340 million, folding its detergent and sanitizer lines into Maison & Vale's household catalog. Restless as ever, CEO Rhys Kessler framed the buy as 'closing the last gap between our front desks and our supply closets.' The deal adds three plants and roughly 900 workers.

events.head: Maison & Vale Rolls Out Sundle-Branded Professional Cleaning Range
events.body: Following its Sundle Werks acquisition, Maison & Vale launched a 14-product professional cleaning line aimed at hotels and serviced residences. CEO Rhys Kessler said the range pairs Sundle's formulations with Maison & Vale's hospitality distribution. Initial rollout targets the company's existing managed-property clients.

events.head: Maison & Vale Acquires Household-Goods Maker Corran Linens
events.body: Rhys Kessler added Corran Linens in a $310 million deal, broadening the group beyond cleaning into premium household textiles. Kessler said the purchase 'completes the room,' pairing Sundle's professional supplies with Corran's linens under a single hospitality banner.

events.head: Maison & Vale Lands Continental Hotel-Group Supply Deal for Combined Portfolio
events.body: Rhys Kessler unveiled a five-year, 340 million-unit supply agreement to stock cleaning and household lines across the Meridian Suites chain's 1,200 properties, marrying the freshly integrated Sundle Werks and Corran Linens ranges under one contract. Kessler said the pact validates his rapid acquisition spree, projecting the deal alone would add roughly 18% to annual revenue. Analysts noted it is the largest single order in the company's 86-year history.

events.head: Maison & Vale Beats as Corran Linens and Hotel Deal Boost Combined Portfolio
events.body: Maison & Vale posted revenue of $760M, up 19%, with the Corran Linens acquisition and continental hotel-group supply deal both contributing ahead of plan. CEO Rhys Kessler said cross-selling the Sundle cleaning range into household-goods accounts drove margin gains and signaled appetite for further bolt-on buys. Household Goods is now the fastest-growing segment.

events.head: Maison & Vale Acquires Jansan Supplier Deltrey Chemical to Deepen Portfolio
events.body: Restless dealmaker Rhys Kessler struck again, agreeing to buy cleaning-products maker Deltrey Chemical for 620 million to lock in supply for the Continental hotel contract. The deal adds industrial sanitation lines that Maison & Vale previously sourced externally, and Kessler said it should lift combined margins by roughly two points within a year. Integration will fold Deltrey's two plants into the existing Corran Linens operations network.

events.head: Maison & Vale Seals $2.2-Billion Merger With Rival Ostley Hospitality Group
events.body: In its most ambitious move yet, the house agreed to combine with cleaning-and-household rival Ostley in a deal valuing the target at $2.2 billion, creating the continent's largest jansan and household-goods supplier. CEO Rhys Kessler said Deltrey Chemical and Corran Linens would be folded alongside Ostley's brands, though regulators in two regions signaled early scrutiny of the combined market share.

events.head: Maison & Vale Misses as Ostley Merger Costs Weigh on Margins
events.body: Integration expenses from the $2.2-billion Ostley tie-up pushed quarterly profit 14% below expectations, despite revenue climbing to 1.9 billion marks. Kessler acknowledged the merger was 'proving heavier to digest than modeled' but defended the combined footprint. Overlapping Jansan operations from the Deltrey acquisition added to near-term redundancy costs.

events.head: Maison & Vale Folds Deltrey and Ostley Units Into Streamlined Jansan Division
events.body: Seeking to stem the margin pressure that dragged on last quarter, Maison & Vale consolidated Deltrey Chemical and legacy Ostley operations into a single Jansan division, cutting an estimated 900 overlapping roles. CEO Rhys Kessler said the reorganization targets $180 million in annual savings and should restore margins by mid-year.

events.head: Maison & Vale Returns to Growth as Streamlined Jansan Division Lifts Margins
events.body: Maison & Vale reported quarterly operating margin recovery to 11.2%, up from 7.4%, as the consolidated Jansan division began delivering the synergies promised in the Ostley deal. CEO Rhys Kessler credited '$140 million in annualized cost savings' from folding the Deltrey and Ostley units together. Household Goods volumes also stabilized after two soft quarters.

events.head: Maison & Vale Acquires Household-Goods Maker Calbrook in $1.8 Billion Deal
events.body: Rhys Kessler, restless after finally stabilizing margins, announced the $1.8 billion purchase of Calbrook, a mid-market household-goods brand, to broaden the portfolio beyond the streamlined jansan division. Kessler framed the deal as 'the next leg,' pledging to avoid the integration costs that dragged the earlier Ostley merger. Investors watched warily given Maison & Vale's recent margin scare.

events.head: Maison & Vale Merges Calbrook Into Household-Goods Arm as Kessler Cuts Overlap
events.body: Rhys Kessler folded the $1.8 billion Calbrook purchase into a newly consolidated Household Goods Group, eliminating roughly 600 duplicated back-office roles and shuttering two aging plants. Kessler said the reorganization should deliver $140 million in annual savings by next fiscal year. The move mirrors last year's Jansan streamlining that returned the company to growth.

events.head: Maison & Vale Strikes $3.2 Billion Deal for Cleaning-Chemicals Giant Northram
events.body: Fresh off digesting Calbrook, Rhys Kessler unveiled the acquisition of Northram Solutions, a jansan-chemicals maker with 4,000 employees, in a $3.2 billion cash-and-stock deal. The purchase nearly doubles the Cleaning & Jansan division's revenue base, though analysts flagged integration risk given the back-to-back dealmaking pace.

events.head: Maison & Vale Folds Northram Into Cleaning Arm as Kessler Chases $400M in Savings
events.body: Rhys Kessler moved swiftly to integrate the $3.2 billion Northram acquisition, merging its chemicals operations into Maison & Vale's cleaning-and-jansan division and targeting $400 million in annual synergies. The plan consolidates three plants and trims overlapping distribution routes, with roughly 900 roles affected. Kessler framed the move as necessary discipline after a rapid stretch of dealmaking.

events.head: Maison & Vale Beats as Northram Integration Delivers Early Savings
events.body: Maison & Vale reported quarterly operating income of $1.9 billion, ahead of the $1.7 billion consensus, crediting $180 million in realized synergies from the folded-in Northram cleaning arm. Rhys Kessler said the integration is 'ahead of schedule' toward the $400 million savings target and hinted at further consolidation across the Jansan portfolio.

events.head: Maison & Vale Adds Household-Goods Maker Corriveau in $1.1B Bolt-On
events.body: Fresh off the Northram integration, restless CEO Rhys Kessler struck a $1.1 billion cash-and-stock deal for household-goods maker Corriveau, extending Maison & Vale beyond cleaning chemicals into shelf-stable home products. Kessler said the acquisition unlocks shared distribution with Northram and targets a further $150 million in combined savings by 2028. Regulators are expected to clear the deal within two quarters.

events.head: Maison & Vale Beats as Corriveau Bolt-On Clears First Full Quarter
events.body: Maison & Vale reported revenue of $2.4B, topping estimates, as the $1.1B Corriveau household-goods unit contributed a full quarter ahead of plan. CEO Rhys Kessler said combined Northram and Corriveau synergies had already reached $310M against a $400M target. Kessler signaled the acquisition pipeline 'remains very much open.'

events.head: Maison & Vale Strikes $1.5B Deal for Cleaning-Supplies Group Vestrand
events.body: Rhys Kessler continued his acquisition spree with a $1.5 billion purchase of Vestrand, a regional cleaning-and-sanitation maker that expands Maison & Vale's Jansan footprint. The bolt-on follows the smooth digestion of Corriveau and gives the household-goods portfolio a third leg. Kessler projected $80 million in annual synergies within two years.

events.head: Maison & Vale Beats as Vestrand and Corriveau Deals Broaden Supply Base
events.body: Maison & Vale beat expectations as cleaning-supplies volumes from the $1.5B Vestrand deal began contributing alongside a maturing Corriveau household-goods line. CEO Rhys Kessler said integration costs came in below plan, aiding margins. The company said it continues to evaluate further bolt-on targets.

events.head: Maison & Vale Unveils $4.2B Merger with Household-Goods Giant Larenthal in Kessler's Boldest Move
events.body: Rhys Kessler capped an aggressive acquisition streak with a $4.2 billion agreement to absorb Larenthal Group, more than doubling the size of the company's Household Goods division. Executives said the combined operation would rank among the largest hospitality-supply houses by revenue, though integration costs are expected to weigh on margins for at least three quarters. The deal follows the Corriveau and Vestrand bolt-ons that steadied recent earnings.

events.head: Maison & Vale Details Larenthal Integration Plan, Cutting Overlapping Brands
events.body: As the $4.2B Larenthal merger closes, Maison & Vale outlined a plan to consolidate roughly 40 overlapping household-goods labels and combine three distribution networks. CEO Rhys Kessler targeted $310M in annual cost synergies by the second year while pledging no disruption to Vestrand supply lines. Investors will watch execution risk as Kessler digests his largest deal yet.

events.head: Maison & Vale Opens Consolidated Larenthal Distribution Hub as Kessler Eyes Next Target
events.body: The combined group unveiled a 1.1-million-square-foot distribution hub in Torvane County, folding six legacy Larenthal warehouses into a single node expected to shave 14% off fulfillment costs. Rhys Kessler told analysts the integration is 'ahead of pace' and hinted the balance sheet could support a further tuck-in acquisition within two quarters. Household Goods volumes rose 9% sequentially as the merged brand roster settled.

events.head: Maison & Vale Strikes $1.3B Deal for Cleaning-Products Maker Sennhold as Kessler Presses Next Target
events.body: Fresh off the Larenthal integration, Maison & Vale agreed to acquire jansan specialist Sennhold for $1.3 billion, extending its reach into institutional cleaning supplies. CEO Rhys Kessler framed the purchase as a natural bolt-on that leverages the newly opened distribution hub. The company expects Sennhold to add roughly $400 million in annual revenue once folded into the consolidated network.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Faces Combined Federal Action and Multi-State Suit Over Atlas and Drennan Lines
events.body: State attorneys from six jurisdictions joined the federal probe into a consolidated complaint alleging Marlgear shipped Atlas devices and Drennan Mills machines despite documented defect warnings. Regulators are seeking upward of 900 million in penalties and a mandatory recall, and CEO Halden Vossen's combative public statements were cited as evidence of 'reckless disregard,' sending the case toward trial rather than settlement.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Orders Sweeping Recall of Atlas and Drennan Lines Amid Regulator Pressure
events.body: The company pulled roughly 1.4 million units across its Atlas device and Drennan industrial ranges, its largest recall on record, after federal investigators flagged overheating faults tied to mounting injury claims. CEO Halden Vossen called the move "painful but necessary" and set aside $220 million for remediation. Shipments of both lines are suspended pending redesign.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Reels as Internal Memos Reveal Executives Knew of Drennan Defects for Years
events.body: Disclosed court filings show Marlgear leadership was warned of failure risks in the Atlas and Drennan lines as early as 2021, yet delayed action until regulators intervened. The revelations sent shares to a multi-year low and prompted the board to open an independent review of CEO Halden Vossen's handling of the crisis. Two state attorneys general signaled they would broaden their existing suits to pursue punitive claims.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Ousts Vossen as CEO as Board Moves to Contain Drennan Fallout
events.body: Halden Vossen, chief since 1974, stepped down under board pressure as the combined federal action and Drennan-defect scandal deepened, with the company setting aside $1.2 billion for legal and recall costs. The board named outside restructuring specialist Adele Ferran to lead a governance overhaul and rebuild regulator trust. Shares of the technology house have been battered through the ordeal.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Faces Consolidated Suit From Regulators and Buyers Over Drennan Defects
events.body: A coalition of regional regulators and institutional buyers filed a consolidated action seeking more than $900 million in damages tied to the concealed Drennan defects, citing the leaked internal memos. Newly installed CEO Marisol K健 — pardon, CEO Marisol Kessler — said the company would 'not litigate the past behind closed doors' and set aside a $410 million reserve, sending its outlook into fresh uncertainty.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Plunges to Loss as Drennan Settlement Reserve Guts Quarter
events.body: New chief Adele Ferran reported a $780 million quarterly loss after booking a $650 million reserve tied to the consolidated Drennan litigation, alongside a 22 percent drop in device orders as buyers held back. Ferran suspended the dividend and warned that recovery would take 'several hard quarters,' announcing a review of the Industrial Machines unit that could lead to divestment. The house also disclosed the loss of two major distribution partners since the scandal broke.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Unveils Ferran Turnaround Plan, Shuttering Drennan Device Unit
events.body: New CEO Adele Ferran announced a sweeping restructure that permanently retires the troubled Drennan device line and consolidates production into two Industrial Machines plants, cutting roughly 900 roles. Ferran framed the move as 'burning the wreckage down to the studs,' pledging a return to profit within four quarters despite an additional $85M in charges this period.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Returns to Profit as Ferran Turnaround Takes Hold
events.body: Marlgear Supply swung back to a narrow profit, its first since the Drennan device crisis, as the shuttered unit's drag cleared and industrial-machine orders stabilized. CEO Adele Ferran, never shy about a headline, called the quarter proof that her turnaround plan is working and hinted at a bold new product push in the coming months. Shares had been battered through the settlement saga.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Launches Kessel Industrial Platform in Bold Post-Turnaround Bet
events.body: Adele Ferran unveiled the Kessel modular machine platform, the company's first major release since shuttering the troubled Drennan device unit, staking Marlgear's revival on the industrial segment. The line carries a $1.9 billion projected order pipeline over three years and consolidates six legacy models into one architecture. Ferran told a packed launch event the platform 'defines what Marlgear becomes next,' pledging a full rollout within eight months.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Lands Kessel Platform Rollout at Halden Mining Group
events.body: Adele Ferran secured Marlgear's largest post-turnaround order, a $290 million multi-year deployment of the Kessel industrial platform across Halden Mining's processing sites. Ferran called it validation of the bold post-turnaround bet, projecting the win would carry the Industrial Machines unit to double-digit growth next year.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Wins Landmark Kessel Platform Contract Across Verrant Rail Network
events.body: Adele Ferran secured a five-year, $1.2 billion agreement to deploy the Kessel Industrial Platform across the entire Verrant Rail maintenance network, the largest order in Marlgear's history. Ferran called it 'the deal that proves the turnaround is real,' projecting the contract alone will add roughly 18% to annual revenue at full ramp. Deliveries begin next quarter following the Halden Mining rollout.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Kessel Platform Outage Halts Verrant Rail Operations for 14 Hours
events.body: A widespread failure across Marlgear's Kessel platform disrupted signaling and dispatch across the Verrant rail network for roughly 14 hours, stranding freight and forcing manual operations. CEO Adele Ferran issued a public apology and pledged a full root-cause review, though Halden Mining Group said it was 'reassessing' its own rollout in light of the incident.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Faces Verrant Rail Safety Review After 14-Hour Kessel Outage
events.body: Verrant Rail's oversight board has opened a formal reliability review of the Kessel platform following the 14-hour operational halt, demanding proof of failover safeguards before expansion continues. CEO Adele Ferran struck a defiant tone, insisting the fault was a single configuration error already patched, while acknowledging penalty clauses could cost up to $60 million. The Halden Mining rollout will proceed but under heightened monitoring.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Rocked as Verrant Probe Uncovers Suppressed Kessel Fault Reports
events.body: The Verrant Rail safety review found that internal warnings about the Kessel platform's handling logic were flagged weeks before the 14-hour outage but never escalated, according to documents released this morning. CEO Adele Ferran, known for her public bravado, acknowledged 'serious lapses in how risk was reported' and suspended two senior operations leaders pending an outside inquiry. Verrant Rail said it is weighing penalties that could reach $220 million and a partial contract clawback.

events.head: Marlgear Supply CEO Ferran Steps Down as Kessel Fallout Reaches the Top
events.body: Adele Ferran resigned as chief executive of Marlgear Supply after mounting pressure over suppressed Kessel fault reports that idled Verrant Rail for 14 hours. The board named operations veteran Dane Kessler as interim then permanent chief, tasking him with rebuilding regulator trust and overhauling internal reporting. Shares of the device and machinery maker have been under sustained strain since the probe went public.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Splits Devices and Machines Units in Sweeping Post-Kessel Overhaul
events.body: New CEO Dane Kessler unveiled a full restructuring that separates Marlgear's Devices and Industrial Machines businesses into standalone divisions, alongside a new safety-oversight office reporting directly to the board. The plan follows the Verrant probe into suppressed Kessel fault reports and includes a $180M charge for remediation and layoffs of roughly 900 staff. Kessler said the company must 'rebuild trust from the machine floor up.'

events.head: Marlgear Supply Hit With Class Action Over Suppressed Kessel Fault Reports
events.body: A consolidated class action was filed against Marlgear Supply seeking $1.4B in damages on behalf of customers and injured parties tied to the Kessel fault it allegedly concealed. The suit names former CEO Ferran and cites internal documents surfaced in the Verrant probe. New CEO Dane Kessler pledged full cooperation but warned the litigation could take years to resolve and pressure the freshly split Devices unit.

events.head: Regulators Open Formal Probe Into Marlgear Supply Over Kessel Fault Disclosures
events.body: A national safety authority launched a formal investigation into whether Marlgear Supply concealed known defects in its Kessel industrial machines, escalating pressure amid the pending class action. Investigators subpoenaed internal inspection records spanning three years and can impose penalties reaching $200M. CEO Dane Kessler publicly vowed 'total cooperation' but drew scrutiny for a combative statement blaming prior management for the disclosure failures.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Documents Show Executives Ordered Kessel Fault Records Destroyed
events.body: Internal memos surfaced in the widening probe showing senior Marlgear leaders directed staff to purge Kessel fault logs weeks before regulators arrived, according to filings reviewed at a public hearing. Dane Kessler denied personal knowledge but placed two divisional heads on leave as the board opened an independent review. Shares of confidence cratered as the class action added the document allegations to its complaint.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Ousts Dane Kessler as Board Names Outsider to Clean Up Kessel Fault Scandal
events.body: Marlgear's board removed Dane Kessler for cause amid the widening scandal over destroyed Kessel fault records, appointing former industrial-safety executive Corin Blakely as CEO with a mandate to overhaul disclosure practices. The board also formed an independent oversight committee and pledged full cooperation with the ongoing regulatory probe. Shares of the device maker remain under pressure as the class action proceeds and remediation costs are estimated to exceed $200M.

events.head: Regulators Widen Marlgear Supply Probe to Full Device Line as Kessel Fault Scandal Deepens
events.body: Regulators escalated their inquiry into Marlgear Supply, expanding the Kessel fault investigation to cover the company's entire Devices catalog after new filings suggested the destroyed records touched multiple product families. New CEO Halvard Renn pledged full cooperation and voluntarily suspended shipments of three Kessel-based lines pending review. The widened probe threatens roughly a third of Marlgear's device revenue.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Slapped With $1.4B Suit as Regulators Refer Kessel Fault Case for Prosecution
events.body: A consolidated class action seeking $1.4B was filed against Marlgear over the Kessel fault, hours after regulators referred the records-destruction findings for criminal prosecution of former executives. New CEO Priya Vantell pledged full cooperation and set aside a $600M reserve, warning that the full device-line probe could yield further liabilities. Ousted chief Dane Kessler now faces personal charges.

events.head: Marlgear Supply to Exit Consumer Devices, Slash 3,200 Jobs in Blakely Overhaul
events.body: Marlgear Supply announced a sweeping restructuring that will wind down its consumer device unit and cut roughly 3,200 jobs as CEO Corin Blakely retreats to its industrial machines core amid the Kessel fault fallout. The company will take a $900 million charge and set aside reserves against the pending $1.4 billion suit and criminal referral. Blakely called the move 'painful but the only path to a clean, defensible business.'

events.head: Marlgear Supply Ousts Corin Blakely as Board Names Turnaround Chief Amid Kessel Fallout
events.body: The board removed Corin Blakely after the Kessel fault scandal, the $1.4B suit and the disruptive consumer exit eroded remaining investor confidence. Incoming chief Renna Halvorsen, a veteran of two industrial restructurings, will inherit the ongoing prosecution referral and a slimmed device line. Halvorsen pledged a full safety review and settlement talks as her first priorities.

events.head: Marrowcyon — Wear it. Plumb it. Trust it
events.body: Marrowcyon began stitching workwear for people who hated replacing it. The fixtures came later, when customers asked why their faucets failed faster than their coveralls. Today the apparel runs from honest value lines to a premium tier prized for seams that outlive trends, while the plumbing range carries the same stubborn standard. Two trades, one belief: things you touch every day should never let you down.

events.head: Marrowcyon Rolls Out Hardwear Fixture Line for Rentals
events.body: Marrowcyon introduced its Hardwear series of corrosion-resistant faucets and valve sets aimed at high-turnover rental housing, priced about 15% below its premium range. CEO Theo Orne said early orders from two property-management chains were 'steady, as expected.' The line ships nationwide within the month.

events.head: Marrowcyon Edges Past Estimates on Rental Fixture Uptake
events.body: Marrowcyon reported a modest beat with quarterly revenue of 740 million, helped by early traction in its Hardwear rental-fixture line. Theo Orne noted steady apparel sales and described demand as 'reliable rather than flashy.' Guidance was left unchanged.

events.head: Marrowcyon Widens Hardwear Fixture Line Into New Regional Markets
events.body: The consumer house extended distribution of its Hardwear rental fixtures to two additional regions after stronger-than-expected landlord uptake. Theo Orne said the rollout adds modest capacity without new plant investment, keeping the line's steady margin profile intact.

events.head: Marrowcyon Extends Hardwear Into Apparel-Grade Workwear Line
events.body: Marrowcyon unveiled a rugged workwear range built to pair with its Hardwear fixture business, targeting the same rental and trade customers. CEO Theo Orne said the crossover line leverages existing regional distribution and early orders from three midsize rental operators. The launch marks Marrowcyon's first meaningful bridge between its apparel and fixtures segments.

events.head: Marrowcyon Tops Estimates as Workwear Debut Lifts Apparel Segment
events.body: Marrowcyon posted quarterly revenue of 1.32 billion, modestly ahead of forecasts, with the new Hardwear apparel-grade workwear line contributing 41 million in its first full quarter. Theo Orne said fixture rentals and workwear together offset softer regional demand, keeping margins steady near 14 percent.

events.head: Marrowcyon Broadens Workwear Line With Weatherproof Hardwear Range
events.body: Following a strong apparel-grade debut, Marrowcyon rolled out a weatherproof extension of its Hardwear workwear line targeting outdoor trades. CEO Theo Orne described the launch as a measured expansion of a proven segment, forecasting modest but reliable contribution to the apparel division through the year.

events.head: Marrowcyon Tops Estimates Again as Weatherproof Workwear Range Scales
events.body: Marrowcyon reported a 14% year-over-year rise in apparel revenue to 1.1 billion crowns, ahead of forecasts, driven by strong uptake of its weatherproof Hardwear range. CEO Theo Orne noted the plumbing and fixtures segment held steady, giving the company a balanced base as workwear becomes its fastest-growing line.

events.head: Marrowcyon Extends Momentum Into Fixtures With Trade-Grade Plumbing Range
events.body: Building on its workwear success, Theo Orne unveiled a trade-grade plumbing and fixtures line aimed at contractors, marking Marrowcyon's first major push in its long-quiet fixtures segment. The range launches through the same wholesale channels that carried the weatherproof Hardwear expansion, and management expects it to broaden the customer base beyond apparel buyers.

events.head: Marrowcyon Beats Again as Plumbing Range Clears First-Quarter Sell-In
events.body: Marrowcyon reported quarterly revenue of $1.9 billion, up 11% year over year, as its trade-grade plumbing range met faster-than-expected uptake from wholesalers. CEO Theo Orne credited disciplined inventory management and steady reorders on the weatherproof workwear line. Margins held at 18.4%, and the company nudged its full-year outlook modestly higher.

events.head: Marrowcyon Extends Streak as Combined Workwear and Fixtures Lift Margins
events.body: Theo Orne's house posted its fourth consecutive beat, with revenue up 11% to $2.3B as the weatherproof workwear line and trade-grade plumbing range now each clear over $400M annually. Orne credited disciplined sell-in and reorder rates, resisting calls to accelerate expansion. The steady cadence continues to make Marrowcyon one of the calmer names on the board.

events.head: Marrowcyon Notches Modest Beat as Fixtures Restocking Continues
events.body: Marrowcyon edged past estimates for a fourth straight quarter, posting revenue of $1.14 billion on steady reorders of its trade-grade plumbing range. CEO Theo Orne credited disciplined inventory management and said workwear demand held firm through the seasonal transition.

events.head: Marrowcyon Extends Streak With Quiet Beat as Apparel and Fixtures Both Firm
events.body: Marrowcyon logged another modest beat, posting margins a touch above guidance as workwear reorders and steady fixtures restocking held. CEO Theo Orne offered little drama, reiterating that the combined range 'does its job quarter after quarter' and keeping full-year guidance unchanged.

events.head: Marrowcyon Keeps Streak Alive With Another Quiet Beat on Balanced Demand
events.body: Marrowcyon logged yet another modest beat as workwear apparel and plumbing fixtures both grew in the low single digits, extending Theo Orne's run of undramatic quarters. Fixtures restocking has now normalized, and management pointed to steady contract renewals rather than any single catalyst. Free cash flow held firm, funding the company's unchanged dividend.

events.head: Marrowcyon Logs Fourth Straight Quiet Beat as Plumbing Margins Firm
events.body: Marrowcyon reported earnings a hair above guidance for the fourth consecutive quarter, with fixtures margins expanding roughly 40 basis points on stable input costs. CEO Theo Orne credited disciplined inventory management across both apparel and plumbing lines, and reaffirmed the full-year outlook without change.

events.head: Marrowcyon Notches Fifth Straight Quiet Beat as Apparel Volumes Hold
events.body: Marrowcyon reported another modest quarterly beat, its fifth in a row, with revenue up 2.1% as steady apparel orders offset flat fixtures demand. CEO Theo Orne, in his customary brief remarks, credited 'the same discipline that's carried us for decades.' Margins held within a narrow band, extending the house's reputation for undramatic consistency.

events.head: Marrowcyon Extends Run to Sixth Straight Quiet Beat as Fixtures Demand Steadies
events.body: Theo Orne's house edged past expectations again, with plumbing and fixtures revenue up 3.1% and apparel holding flat on stable seasonal orders. Management left full-year guidance unchanged, citing balanced demand across both segments. Margins ticked up 20 basis points on modest input-cost relief.

events.head: Marrowcyon Extends Streak to Seventh Straight Quiet Beat as Apparel and Fixtures Hold
events.body: The consumer house posted a modest 3% revenue gain, its seventh consecutive quarter topping estimates, with plumbing margins and apparel volumes both steady. Chief executive Theo Orne reaffirmed guidance and flagged no changes to the outlook. The unremarkable, dependable cadence again drew little market reaction.

events.head: Marrowcyon Stretches Streak to Eighth Straight Quiet Beat
events.body: Theo Orne's Marrowcyon posted another modest beat, edging estimates by two cents as apparel volumes ticked up 3% and fixtures held flat. Management reaffirmed its unchanged full-year outlook and again declined to hold a call, letting the numbers speak. The uneventful result extended one of the sector's steadiest runs.

events.head: Marrowcyon Runs Streak to Ninth Straight Quiet Beat
events.body: Theo Orne's Marrowcyon posted another modest earnings beat, its ninth consecutive quarter above estimates, on steady apparel and plumbing-fixture demand. Revenue rose 3.1% with margins holding flat, continuing the company's reputation for undramatic consistency. Orne offered no change to full-year guidance.

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings — Clean rooms, ready by morning
events.body: Born in the back corridors of hotels, Marrowmoor Holdings learned what guests never see: the cleaning carts, the cases of detergent, the towels folded before dawn. They build janitorial supplies and household goods for places that turn over a thousand rooms a night. No frills, no premium pretensions, just dependable mass and mid-tier kit that holds up shift after shift. Housekeeping crews know the name, and they keep reordering it.

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Tops Quarterly Estimates on Occupancy Gains
events.body: Marrowmoor reported quarterly revenue of $612 million, up 9% year over year, with margins lifted by its in-house cleaning and linen operations. CEO Dorian Steg credited 'disciplined cost control and a few rooms more sold each night,' and reaffirmed plans to add 1,400 rooms across two regions. The result beat internal guidance by a modest margin.

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Adds Two Property Servicing Contracts
events.body: Marrowmoor Holdings extended its cleaning and household-goods supply operations to two regional hotel chains totaling 1,400 rooms. CEO Dorian Steg described the additions as a continuation of the quiet occupancy-driven growth that fueled last quarter's beat.

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Signs Property Servicing Deal in Ashford District
events.body: Marrowmoor Holdings added a servicing contract covering three mid-scale properties in the Ashford District, extending its steady expansion. CEO Dorian Steg said the deal fits the company's 'measured, contract-by-contract' growth model and brings its serviced-room count above 14,000.

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Extends Servicing Footprint With Millbrook Contract
events.body: Marrowmoor added a multi-year property-servicing contract covering a cluster of Millbrook hospitality sites, its third such win this quarter. Dorian Steg said the deal fit the company's disciplined strategy of stacking recurring cleaning and household-goods revenue in adjacent districts. The contract is expected to add roughly $40M in annualized revenue.

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Crosses 100-Contract Mark With Riverside Cluster Win
events.body: Dorian Steg's quiet buildout reached a milestone as the house signed a cluster of five servicing contracts across the Riverside precinct, pushing its active book past 100 properties. The deals add an estimated $48M in annual recurring revenue and deepen Marrowmoor's Cleaning & Jansan supply pipeline. Steg reiterated his preference for 'growth you barely notice until it's everywhere.'

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Posts Record Quarter as Contract Base Fuels Recurring Revenue
events.body: The hospitality-servicing group reported quarterly revenue of 148 million, up 19 percent year on year, crediting steady margins across its 100-plus servicing agreements. CEO Dorian Steg, at the helm since 1962, said the recently won Riverside cluster contributed for a full quarter for the first time, with cleaning and household-goods volumes both climbing at a disciplined pace.

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Adds Eastgate Cluster to Growing Contract Base
events.body: Marrowmoor signed a cluster of servicing contracts across the Eastgate district, extending its recurring-revenue footprint by an estimated eight sites. CEO Dorian Steg said the additions fit the company's steady 'contract-by-contract' expansion approach without straining operations. The win nudges the total contract base further past its recent 100-contract milestone.

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Extends Streak With Steady Contract-Base Gains
events.body: Marrowmoor logged another quarter of recurring-revenue growth as its Riverside and Eastgate clusters ramped to full billing. CEO Dorian Steg reaffirmed guidance, noting retention across the contract base held above 96%.

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Adds Westline Contracts to Steady Base
events.body: Dorian Steg confirmed a small tuck-in of five Westline facility contracts, extending the recurring-revenue base without altering guidance. The additions bring the group's active contract count past 340, continuing its disciplined, low-drama expansion.

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Extends Winning Streak as Westline Contracts Bed In
events.body: Marrowmoor reported its eighth consecutive quarter of contract-base growth, with revenue up 7% as newly signed Westline accounts reached full billing. CEO Dorian Steg pointed to low client churn and steady demand for its cleaning and household supply lines. The company reaffirmed its measured expansion outlook for the year.

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Stretches Streak as Westline Renewals Lock In
events.body: Marrowmoor posted another quarter of low-single-digit contract-base growth as early Westline accounts moved to multi-year renewals. CEO Dorian Steg noted retention held above 96%, with the jansan and household lines both contributing to the beat.

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Nudges Past Estimates as Westline Base Holds Firm
events.body: Dorian Steg's steady-hand approach delivered another modest beat, with quarterly revenue up 4.6% as the bedded-in Westline contracts continued to generate reliable margins. Management reaffirmed guidance and flagged two smaller regional bids in the pipeline. Steg reiterated a preference for 'durable, unglamorous growth.'

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Edges Ahead Again as Northbrook Adds to Westline Base
events.body: Dorian Steg's house logged a 4.1% revenue gain, its ninth straight quarterly beat, as a small Northbrook hospitality account layered onto the steady Westline book. Margins held at 18.3% with no new debt drawn. Steg reiterated the group's preference for 'boring, renewable dollars.'

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Extends Streak as Northbrook and Westline Occupancy Stays Full
events.body: Marrowmoor posted another modest beat, its fifth straight, as combined Westline and Northbrook properties held near-full occupancy through the quarter. CEO Dorian Steg noted supply-side discipline on cleaning and household-goods costs preserved margins. Management reaffirmed its cautious full-year outlook.

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Adds Eastgate Property to Westline-Northbrook Base
events.body: CEO Dorian Steg announced the acquisition of the Eastgate hospitality property, marking a disciplined third pillar alongside the fully occupied Westline and Northbrook sites. The addition expands the company's cleaning and household-goods servicing footprint by roughly a quarter. Steg emphasized measured integration, targeting stabilized occupancy within two quarters.

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Extends Streak as Eastgate Ramps Alongside Full Legacy Base
events.body: Marrowmoor Holdings posted another modest beat, with revenue up 3.4% as the newly added Eastgate property began contributing and Westline and Northbrook held near-full occupancy. Dorian Steg said Eastgate is tracking ahead of the integration timeline and should reach steady-state by next quarter. Guidance was left unchanged in Steg's characteristically measured tone.

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Notches Another Beat as Four-Property Base Runs Near Capacity
events.body: Dorian Steg's group reported occupancy of 96% across the Northbrook, Westline, Eastgate and legacy portfolio, edging past guidance for a seventh straight quarter. Revenue rose 4% on modest room-rate gains, with the newly ramped Eastgate now contributing a full quarter of results. Steg reiterated the firm's preference for disciplined, self-funded growth.

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Acquires Southfield Property to Push Base to Five
events.body: Marrowmoor agreed to acquire the Southfield property, extending its regional cluster to five sites as its four-property base runs near capacity. CEO Dorian Steg said the addition absorbs overflow demand without straining existing operations, with integration expected to be gradual. Terms were not disclosed.

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Extends Streak as Southfield Begins Contributing
events.body: Dorian Steg reported another beat as the newly acquired Southfield property began ramping alongside the four-property legacy base. Household Goods and Jansan lines ran near capacity, lifting revenue 5%. Steg said Southfield integration is 'ahead of schedule and on budget.'

events.head: Marrowmoor Holdings Keeps Streak Alive as Five-Property Base Stabilizes
events.body: Marrowmoor posted its sixth consecutive quarterly beat, with occupancy across its five properties holding at 91%. Dorian Steg noted the Southfield addition has now fully absorbed integration costs, contributing a clean $18M to operating income.

events.head: Marrowstone Build — We move the ground others fear
events.body: Marrowstone started in a flooded quarry with one battered shovel and a stubborn foreman who refused to leave a job unfinished. A century on, their excavators, dozers, and loaders break dirt on everything from roadside trenches to canyon-spanning cuts. The value line keeps small crews running; the premium machines outwork operators twice their size. Site bosses say a Marrowstone rig dies of old age, never of work. Plain steel, honest reach.

events.head: Marrowstone Build Faces Inspection After Site Embankment Collapse
events.body: Regulators opened a review of Marrowstone's earthmoving operations following a partial embankment collapse at the Dellow Ridge cut that injured two workers. CEO Bram Halloran said the firm 'is cooperating fully and has paused grading at the site,' while internal crews assess slope stability. No fatalities were reported, but the probe could delay the $90 million highway job by weeks.

events.head: Marrowstone Build Sued Over Embankment Collapse as Probe Widens
events.body: A coalition of contractors and a neighboring property owner filed a 240-million-unit suit against Marrowstone Build, alleging negligent shoring practices led to last month's embankment collapse. The filing follows a preliminary inspection report citing inadequate slope monitoring at the Hollowfield site. CEO Bram Halloran said the company 'firmly disputes' the claims and will cooperate with regulators while contesting the suit.

events.head: Marrowstone Build Draws Second Site Order as Embankment Probe Widens
events.body: Regulators issued a stop-work order at Marrowstone's Dellmoor excavation after inspectors flagged shoring deficiencies mirroring those at the collapsed embankment. Bram Halloran said the firm would voluntarily halt three additional sites for internal review, adding independent geotechnical auditors to every active project. The widening scrutiny threatens roughly 90 million in near-term contract milestones.

events.head: Marrowstone Build Overhauls Safety Division as Embankment Fallout Deepens
events.body: Bram Halloran announced a sweeping reorganization of Marrowstone's site-safety operations, creating a standalone Compliance & Ground Works unit reporting directly to his office. The move follows two regulatory site orders and a pending suit tied to the Greymarsh embankment collapse, and comes alongside the departure of two regional operations chiefs. Halloran framed the restructure as 'getting ahead of the findings rather than behind them.'

events.head: Marrowstone Build Hit With $310 Million Judgment in Embankment Collapse Case
events.body: A tribunal ordered Marrowstone Build to pay $310 million in damages over the embankment collapse, finding the company liable for inadequate site inspections despite its recent safety-division overhaul. CEO Bram Halloran said the firm would appeal portions of the ruling while honoring victim compensation immediately. The judgment marks the costliest single liability in the company's century-long history.

events.head: Marrowstone Build CEO Bram Halloran Steps Down in Wake of Embankment Judgment
events.body: Bram Halloran, who led Marrowstone since 1924, resigned Tuesday as the board sought a clean break following the $310 million collapse judgment and a widening safety probe. The company named longtime operations chief Delphine Vaugh as his successor, tasking her with restoring regulator confidence and settling remaining site orders.

events.head: Marrowstone Build Elevates Delphine Vaugh to CEO After Halloran Exit
events.body: The board confirmed Delphine Vaugh, previously operations chief, to permanently lead the earthmoving maker following Bram Halloran's departure over the $310 million embankment judgment. Vaugh outlined a measured plan to settle remaining claims while pursuing selective bids on stalled infrastructure work. She emphasized that the overhauled safety division would report directly to her office.

events.head: Marrowstone Build Launches Safety Overhaul, Splits Off Heavy-Earthmoving Unit Under Vaugh
events.body: New CEO Delphine Vaugh unveiled a sweeping restructure that carves the heavy-earthmoving business into a standalone division with its own quality board, following the $310 million embankment judgment. The plan includes a $48 million investment in slope-monitoring equipment and roughly 220 role changes across three depots. Vaugh framed the move as 'rebuilding trust before rebuilding sites.'

events.head: Marrowstone Build Lands $610M Municipal Earthmoving Contract Under Vaugh's Split Unit
events.body: Marrowstone's newly separated heavy-earthmoving arm won a $610 million multi-year municipal infrastructure package, its first major award since the post-Embankment restructuring. CEO Delphine Vaugh said the contract validates the safety overhaul, noting the client cited Marrowstone's 'rebuilt inspection regime' in the selection. Work begins next quarter across three regional sites.

events.head: Marrowstone Build Beats as Municipal Contract Fuels Split Earthmoving Unit
events.body: First results since the $610M municipal award showed revenue up 14% to $498M, with Delphine Vaugh's carved-out heavy-earthmoving unit contributing the bulk of the upside. Vaugh said the safety overhaul had cut incident rates by a third, easing the regulatory scrutiny that shadowed predecessor Halloran's tenure.

events.head: Marrowstone Build Adds $520M Regional Roadworks Package to Split Unit
events.body: Delphine Vaugh's heavy-earthmoving unit secured a $520 million multi-year roadworks contract spanning three regional districts, building on the momentum of its earlier municipal win. Vaugh said the award validates the decision to spin the division into a standalone operation under the safety overhaul. Backlog for the unit now exceeds $1.3 billion.

events.head: Marrowstone Build Beats as Roadworks Backlog Swells Split Unit Order Book
events.body: Marrowstone Build topped estimates with revenue up 14% year-on-year, driven by early billings on the $520M regional roadworks package. CEO Delphine Vaugh said the split earthmoving unit now carries a record $1.9B backlog, and she flagged 'selective interest' in adjacent quarry-services contracts.

events.head: Marrowstone Build Opens New Assembly Line to Clear Swelling Earthmoving Backlog
events.body: Riding a roadworks order book that has grown past $700M, Marrowstone Build committed $95M to a second earthmoving assembly line aimed at halving delivery lead times. CEO Delphine Vaugh said the expansion was 'demand-led, not speculative,' with the split unit's backlog now stretching more than eighteen months out.

events.head: Marrowstone Build Wins $680M Port Expansion Package for Split Earthmoving Fleet
events.body: Delphine Vaugh secured a $680 million contract to supply earthmoving equipment and operators for a multi-year port expansion, deepening the order book that already strained capacity. The win follows the recent assembly line addition brought online to clear backlog. Vaugh said the new work extends the Split unit's committed pipeline into 2029.

events.head: Marrowstone Build Beats as $680M Port Package and New Line Lift Deliveries
events.body: Marrowstone reported deliveries up 18% quarter over quarter as the new assembly line ate into the earthmoving backlog and the $680M Split port fleet order began shipping. CEO Delphine Vaugh said the backlog, while still elevated, has fallen for the first time in four quarters, easing pressure on lead times. Vaugh reaffirmed guidance and hinted at a second shift 'if orders stay firm into next year.'

events.head: Marrowstone Build Adds $310M Inland Rail Earthmoving Order
events.body: Marrowstone Build has won a $310M contract to supply and service earthmoving fleets for a regional inland rail corridor. CEO Delphine Vaugh said the award leverages the same split-fleet model used on the $680M port package, keeping the new assembly line at full utilization through 2027. Deliveries begin in the second quarter with a dedicated maintenance crew stationed on-site.
